title: Nuance Skills 1A

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the NUANCE Program

description: Improve social language, social interaction, and appropriate use of executive functioning in order to facilitate positive educational outcomes that will lead to passing credit classes, earning certificates, associate degrees or transferring to universities. ACCS Nuance Skills 1A will introduce the topics of social skills and training for improved academic success. This course will introduce topics such as assessing interests, trading information, disability acceptance and identity, and perspective taking. This is one of a two-part series of classes designed for students that been accepted into Neurodiverse Unique Autistic students in College Education (NUANCE) Program at Mt. SAC. NUANCE is based on PEERS (Program for the Education and Enrichment of Relational Skills) created by UCLA

title: Nuance Skills 1B

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the NUANCE Program

description: Improve social language, social interaction, and appropriate use of executive functioning in order to facilitate positive educational outcomes that will lead to students passing credit classes, earning certificates, associate degrees or transferring to universities. ACCS Nuance Skills 1B will expand and enhance social skills of students for improved independence and academic success. The topics will include adulting skills such as employment readiness, dating, and transportation. This is one of a two-part series of classes designed for students that have been accepted into Neurodiverse Unique Autistic students in College Education (NUANCE) Program at Mt. SAC. NUANCE is based on PEERS (Program for the Education and Enrichment of Relational Skills) created by UCLA.

title: Language Development for Deaf Students in ASL and English
description: Language development to improve written English and American Sign Language (ASL) communication for Deaf or hard of hearing students who use sign language.

title: Language Enhancement for Deaf Students in ASL and English
description: Language enhancement for Deaf or hard of hearing students who use sign language to improve written English and ASL communication.

title: Academic Success Strategies for Students with Disabilities
description: Strategies for academic success intended for students with physical or learning-related disabilities. Addresses techniques to improve language, memory, and reasoning that can be applied to specific courses.

title: Memory Strategies for Students with Disabilities
description: Principles of the memory process as it applies to academic coursework. Focuses on the memory process, improving specific memory components, identifying key concepts to memorize, and the independent application of memory strategies to other academic courses.

title: Strategies for Success in Math for Students with Disabilities
description: Strategies for students currently in math courses for academic success in relationship to disabilities. Emphasis on effects of and strategies for processing, language expression, memory, reasoning, and processing speed as they relate to math.

title: Writing Strategies for Students with Disabilities
description: Strategies for success for students who struggle with writing. These strategies are applied to student's writing assignments by supporting the student's strengths and compensating for their weaknesses in writing.

title: Introduction to Addiction Counseling
description: Presents an overview of substance use and its ramifications. Explores the impact of addiction on an individual's social, psychological, economic, and physiological well-being; as well as community and family functioning. Examines the myths, images, and stereotypes about drugs and drug users. Explores various approaches to recovery. Includes familiarization with terms. Student attendance of a 12 Step meeting is required. This course, in conjunction with AD 3 , meets requirements for AB2473.

title: Physiological Effects of Alcohol and Drugs
description: Examines effects of alcohol and drugs on the human body. Includes tolerance, habituation, cross-tolerance, and synergistic effect.

title: Addiction: Prevention, Intervention, and Recovery
description: Introduces prevention, intervention, and recovery protection strategies for persons experiencing substance use disorder and related problems. Examines evidence-based treatment models, policies, and practices focused on diverse and underserved populations. This course, in conjunction with AD 1 , meets basic skills requirements of AB 2473

title: Issues in Domestic Violence
description: History, law, and psychology of domestic violence. Cultural, social aspects, and relationship to substance abuse explored.

title: Co-Occurring Disorders

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3 and AD 4 (may be taken concurrently)

description: Overview of the complex interactions of mental health and addiction disorders. Reviews and examines the key areas involving co-occurring disorders: definition, diagnosis, treatment, and aftercare.

title: Group Process and Leadership

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3
Corequisite: AD 4 and AD 6 (May have been taken previously)

description: Goals, stages, and processes of group counseling in addiction treatment. The role, responsibilities, and ethics of the group leader are emphasized along with strategies and techniques for facilitating group processes as a means of changing behavior.

title: Family Dynamics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3
Corequisite: AD 4 (may have been taken previously) and AD 6 (may have been taken previously) and AD 15 (may have been taken previously)

description: Explores the multigenerational nature of substance use disorders in family systems with emphasis on the risk factors for addiction, dynamics of dysfunctional families; and the effect of neglect and abuse in the home. Typical norms, values, roles, and beliefs of family systems, adaptation, and treatment strategies will be examined.

title: Case Management and Documentation

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3 and AD 4 and AD 6 and AD 15

description: The importance of case management in complex and diverse client populations and in facilitating comprehensive documentation that meets clinical and legal regulations. Students will gain hands-on experience with a variety of current, industry-accepted documents with an emphasis on state and federal expectations impacting substance abuse treatment records.

title: Techniques of Interviewing and Counseling

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3
Corequisite: AD 4 and AD 6 (May have been taken previously)

description: Introduction to theories, models, and the basic principles of interviewing and counseling that promote helping relationships within a diverse treatment population. Students will learn and practice basic skills in attentive listening, assessing, crisis intervention, and recognizing and responding to different levels of communication as it pertains to paraprofessionals. Specific emphasis is placed on self-awareness and self-care.

title: Laws and Ethics for Addiction Counselors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3
Corequisite: AD 4 and AD 6 (May have been taken previously)

description: This course introduces students to those issues associated with the dignity and worth of individual human beings and the protection of fundamental human rights. Professional ethics, clients' rights, confidentiality, and other relevant material related to the field of addiction will be explored. Topics include discussing situations for setting boundaries, and an overview of current federal legislation pertaining to client confidentiality and release of information.

title: Addiction Counseling Work Experience Seminar

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3 and AD 4 and AD 6 and AD 15

description: Engages students in critical analysis of their strengths and areas for growth as professional addiction counselors. Emphasis on values, building self-awareness, competence, self-care, and preparation to meet certification standards in the State of California. This is a co-requisite course for AD 85 Work Experience in Addiction Counseling.

title: Work Experience in Addiction Counseling

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AD 1 and AD 2 and AD 3 and AD 4 and AD 6 and AD 15 and Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course.

description: Students will gain work experience by observing and performing the core functions of an addiction counselor in a substance abuse treatment program. Students must complete a minimum of 255 hours to pass the course and meet requirements for the addiction counseling certificate and AS degree.

title: The Administration of Justice System
description: History and philosophy of the justice system, subsystems, roles, relationships and theories of crime causation and correction.

title: Principles and Procedures of the Justice System
description: Due process in criminal proceedings from pre-arrest through trial and appeal using statutory law and legal precedent.

title: Concepts of Criminal Law
description: Classification of crime, elements of crimes, common and statutory law, and evidence as observed through the study of case law decisions by state and federal courts.

title: Legal Aspects of Evidence
description: Criminal evidence, including admissibility, witness competency, privileged communication, hearsay, and collection and preservation of evidence.

title: Community Relations
description: Examines the complex, dynamic relationship between communities and the justice system in addressing crime and conflict with an emphasis on the challenges and prospects of administering justice within a diverse multicultural population.

title: Police Patrol Tactics and Strategy
description: Foundation issues of police tactics, operations, and the complex role of the uniform police officer in the community. The history and development of approaches, decision-making processes, and officer conduct evaluation.

title: Introduction to Homeland Security
description: Public management policies and issues relevant to the security of the United States. Roles and responsibilities of federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies. Emphasis on the role of first responders to threats and events through theories, concepts, and case studies.

title: Introduction to Correctional Sciences
description: The philosophy behind past and present practices used in the criminal justice and correctional processes. Includes the analysis of punishment and alternatives including their impact in corrections within the criminal justice system. The examination of the types of clients within correctional institutions and various contemporary correctional issues.

title: Principles of Investigation
description: Investigation, 4th Amendment issues including crime scene search and recording, collection and preservation of physical evidence, modus operandi, suspect profiling scientific aids, sources of information, use of informants, interviews and interrogation, follow up, and case preparation.

title: Narcotics Investigation
description: Investigation and arrest techniques for drug enforcement. Drug effects, use of informants, constitutional issues, and handling of evidence.

title: Introduction to Forensics for Criminal Justice
description: Collecting, preserving, and analyzing physical evidence. Focuses on the reliability of physical evidence for the purpose of establishing facts and proof.

title: Gangs and Corrections
description: Contemporary street and prison gang issues, including historical and current perspectives, gang dynamics, identification of characteristics, and cultural differences of gang philosophy. Includes law enforcement and correction's role in intervention and suppression.

title: Administration of Justice Report Writing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Eligibility for ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Techniques for proper documentation of crime reports and related law enforcement records. Use of simulations and role-playing.

title: Work Experience in Administration of Justice

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.

description: Provides actual on-the-job experience at an approved work site which is related to classroom instruction in Administration of Justice. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit. If this is a volunteer program on or off campus, a minimum number hours per month will be required as part of the 54 hour total. Students who repeat this course will have an opportunity to create a performance contract with a supervisor and the end of the course which will detail specific learning objectives to achieve during the next phase.

title: Introduction to Aviation Careers
description: Aviation industry career preparation for pilots, air traffic controllers, aircraft dispatchers, aircraft maintenance technicians, flight attendants, airport operation specialists, airport security specialists, and unmanned aircraft specialists. In this course students will explore the fundamentals of aircraft operations, as well as history and development of the aviation industry. Students will also explore and learn the requirements for completing the Associate degree in commercial flight, aviation science, and other degrees. This course is developed in conjunction with industry partners to address emerging industry needs. Field trips may be required for completion of this course.

title: Primary Pilot Ground School
description: Aerodynamics, aircraft performance, Federal Aviation Regulations, aviation weather factors, and cross-country navigation procedures; provides introductory material on radio navigation, aeromedical factors, and radio communications procedures. Meets the preparation requirements for the FAA Private Pilot knowledge examination and FAA Air Traffic Control Basics.

title: Aviation Weather
description: Weather elements, atmosphere, weather mechanics, weather disturbances, weather analysis and forecasts. Evaluation of aviation weather reports and forecasts.

title: Federal Aviation Regulations
description: Federal Aviation Regulations (FAR), pertaining to pilot certification, aircraft maintenance, and general operating rules. Air traffic control practices and procedures and reporting of aircraft accidents.

title: Flying Team Fundamentals - Regionals

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Member of the Mt. SAC Flying Team

description: Participation in one or more Regional competitions in the National Intercollegiate Flying Association (NIFA). Instructions in preparatory procedures for these competitions include techniques in aviation academic testing and basic level understanding of flight events. Competition and practice attendance required outside of regularly scheduled class hours. Students who repeat this course will benefit from additional competition experiences. Field trips are required.

title: Flying Team Fundamentals - Nationals

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Member of the Mt. SAC Flying Team

description: Participation in one or more National, or similar competitions in the National Intercollegiate Flying Association (NIFA) Instruction in preparatory procedures for these competitions include techniques for success in precision and accuracy flying for flight events including: air navigation, message drop, and accuracy landings. Competition and practice attendance required outside of regularly scheduled class hours. Students who repeat this course will benefit from additional National, or similar competition experiences. Field trips are required.

title: Commercial Pilot Ground School
description: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Commercial Pilot certification requirements, including aerodynamics, commercial pilot maneuvers, complex aircraft operations, multi-engine aircraft operations, aircraft weight and balance, aircraft performance charts, and radio navigation using advanced instrumentation. Prepares students for completion of the FAA Commercial Pilot Computerized Knowledge Examination.

title: Air Transportation
description: Survey course of the air transportation industry. Topics include an introduction to air transportation, structure and economics of the airlines, general aviation operations, and aviation career planning.

title: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Basic
description: Piloting of Unmanned Aircraft Systems. This class includes instruction toward Remote Pilot certification Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Part 107 licensing. Students will receive instruction on the principles of operating unmanned aircraft systems, pre-flight, flight, and post-flight operations and procedures. Meets the preparation requirements for the FAA Remote Pilot knowledge examination. Field trips are required for this course.

title: Unmanned Aircraft Commercial Operations
description: Advanced skills in commercial uncrewed aircraft system operations. Topics include commercial applications of UAS and robotics, safety management, safety policy, risk management, safety culture, emergency preparation, project assessment, flight planning, current regulations and production of customer deliverables.

title: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Advanced Operations
description: Advanced skills in planning and operating unmanned aircraft systems for beyond visual line of sight and nighttime operations. Topics include managing risk, performing flight operations, selecting platforms and sensors. Field trips are required.

title: Unmanned Aircraft Build
description: Build unmanned aircraft. Use aircraft engineering design processes. Topics include methods and strategies for fabrication of fixed wing and multicopter aircraft, hand tool use, build techniques, materials selection, testing, and troubleshooting. Field trips are required.

title: Aviation Safety and Human Factors
description: Evaluation and analysis of factors leading to aircraft accidents as it relates to the environment of the pilot and air traffic controller.

title: Aircraft and Engines
description: Aircraft design, subsystems, repair, and maintenance. Principles of internal combustion engines, fuel system, engine construction and design, lubrication and cooling methods, ignition system, and basic troubleshooting. Turbine engine basic design and operational characteristics.

title: Unmanned Aircraft Systems Advanced
description: Advanced skills in operating unmanned aircraft systems. Topics include analyzing flight characteristics, utilizing flight planning software, sensor selection and software use, spectrum analysis, safety practices and risk analysis, incident reporting, and data analysis. Field trips are required.

title: Navigation
description: Dead reckoning navigation procedures. Aeronautical computers and their application in cross-country flying. Use of radio navigation aids, flight planning, flight directors, global positioning system, and electronic flight instrumentation systems.

title: Instrument Ground School
description: Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), Air Traffic Control communications and procedures, air navigation radio aids, instrument landing systems, flight instruments, aircraft performance, aeronautical publications, instrument approach procedures, IFR cross-country navigation, and instrument weather. Meets the preparation requirements for the FAA Instrument Pilot computerized knowledge exam.

title: Aircraft Dispatcher Operations

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AERO 100 and AERO 102 and AERO 104 and AERO 150 and AERO 152 and AERO 200 and AERO 202 and AERO 250 and AERO 252

description: Elements and techniques of aircraft dispatch operations. Includes aircraft dispatcher briefings to a simulated flight crew. This course prepares students to enter employment as a certified aircraft dispatcher in the airline industry, air-medical industry, corporate aircraft operators, and aviation weather service companies. Successful completion of this course enables students to take the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) written, oral, and practical tests for the FAA Aircraft Dispatcher Certificate. Students who pass the FAA Aircraft Dispatcher Knowledge Test will qualify to take the FAA Oral and Practical Examination for the FAA aircraft dispatcher certificate.

title: Flight Instructor Ground School

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AERO 100 and AERO 104 and AERO 150

description: Basic teaching principles and application of those principles in teaching student pilots. Analysis of flight maneuvers and instruments. Prepares students for Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) knowledge tests for Flight Instructors.

title: Large Aircraft Systems
description: This Boeing 737-NG aircraft course is designed for students desiring to become pilots, aircraft dispatchers, or technicians on large aircraft typically flown in the airline industry. Design features and operational characteristics with emphasis on aircraft and engine systems. Off-campus trips are required.

title: Work Experience in Aeronautics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.

description: Provides on-the-job experience in aeronautics at an approved work site which is related to classroom instruction. A minimum of five hours per week of supervised work 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit.

title: Introduction to Black Studies
description: This interdisciplinary survey course broadly and deeply approaches the heterogeneous experience of Black life in the United States through analysis of the historical, political, social, economic, educational, and cultural experiences and expressions of Black people. This course is largely constructed around the words and voices used by Black people to inspire, and effect change in the United States. Key topics covered are: African Origins, African Diaspora, colonization, race, racialization, anti-Black racism, identity, white supremacy, power, slavery, education, mass incarceration, cultural expression, Jim Crow, migration, Civil Rights, Black Empowerment, Black Feminist discourse, Black Queer discourse, resistance, equity, self-determination, decolonization, liberation movements, and the intersection of racial, ethnic, gender, and sexual identities..

title: Veterinary Office Procedures

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A ) and ( COMM C1000 or SPCH 1A) or (COMM C1000H or SPCH 1AH)

description: Veterinary medical records, client relations, medical terminology, filing of governmental reports, legal responsibilities of registered veterinary technicians, and veterinary medical ethics.

title: Medical Nursing and Animal Care

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 62A and AGHE 64 and AGHE 86 . Rabies vaccination series or titer required. See notes in Course Description below.

description: Animal examination for health and disease conditions in the animal hospital, including sanitation, administration of medicine, emergency treatment, therapeutic techniques, dental prophylaxis, venipuncture, electrocardiology, and application of casts, splints, and other appliances. Includes diseases both infectious and zoonotic, their causes and effects, and immunology of animals. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by Board Policy & Administrative Procedure 5210 and requirements mandated by American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA). The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at document submission instructions https://www.mtsac.edu/vettech/immunizations.html . Additional information available at Centers for Disease Control (CDC) information and AVMA accreditation policies.

title: Animal Surgical Nursing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 60 and Rabies vaccination series or titer required. See notes in Course Description below.

description: Surgical preparation, surgical assistance, post-operative care, administering and monitoring anesthesia, dentistry, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), sterilization, and the maintenance of a sterile environment. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by Board Policy 5210 and Administrative Procedure 5210 and requirements mandated by the American Veterinary Medical Association. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at https://www.mtsac.edu/vettech/immunizations.html. Additional information available at CDC Information and AVMA policies .

title: Clinical Pathology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 86 and CHEM 40 and MICR 1 or MICR 22

description: Hematology, clinical chemistries, internal parasites, immunology, serology, and vaginal cytology of domestic animals.

title: Clinical Pathology B
description: Bacteriology, clinical chemistry, urinalysis, external parasites, and cytology of domestic animals.

title: Veterinary Pharmacology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 86 and MATH 130 or MATH 160 or MATH 180

description: Pharmaceuticals and biologics commonly used in the maintenance of animal health. Includes generic terminology, abbreviations for prescriptions, labeling requirements, state and federal laws, classification of materials, weights and measures, drug dosage flow rates, pharmacological mathematics and the metric system, side effects, and drug interactions.

title: Veterinary Radiography

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGAN 51 or ASCI 51 and AGHE 64 and AGHE 86 and rabies vaccination series or titer required. See notes in Course Description below.

description: Concepts and skills of veterinary positioning of canine, feline, avian, reptilian species, and livestock for radiography; processing of the radiograph; radiation safety; technique and instrumentation; contrast radiography, dental radiology and advanced imaging such as ultrasound, MRI, CT scan, nuclear isotopes scans. Emphasizes performance of x-ray procedures for the veterinary practitioner. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by BP & AP 5210 and requirements mandated by American Veterinary Medical Association. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at document submission instructions. Additional information available at CDC information and AVMA accreditation policies.

title: Laboratory Animal Medicine and Care
description: Laboratory animal medicine, care, and procedures. Rules and regulations governing laboratory animals.

title: Applied Animal Health Procedures

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 64 and ASCI 51 . Rabies vaccination series or titer required. See notes in Course Description below.

description: A field study course that emphasizes practical experience in applied clinical procedures and techniques, including treatments, preventive health care, and minor surgical procedures with school owned domestic farm animals. Experiences with animals will vary due to seasonal changes and different husbandry practices during fall and spring. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by BP & AP 5210 and requirements mandated by American Veterinary Medical Association. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at document submission instructions. Additional information available at CDC information and AVMA accreditation policies.

title: Seminar in Registered Veterinary Technology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 61 and Completion of the Registered Veterinary Technology program.

description: Prepares students for Veterinary Technician National Exam (VTNE). Includes exposure to the types of questions encountered in registration examinations, question analysis strategies, and review of important anatomical, physiological, and nursing concepts.

title: Anatomy and Physiology of Domestic Animals

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: BIOL 4 or BIOL 4H . Rabies vaccine required. See notes below.

description: Analyzes the body structures and systems, comparing domestic animals commonly found in veterinary medicine. The physiology section emphasizes functions of internal organs and body systems. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by BP & AP 5210 and requirements mandated by American Veterinary Medical Association. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at https://www.mtsac.edu/vettech/immunizations.html . Additional information available at CDC Information and AVMA policies.

title: Work Experience in Registered Veterinary Technology - Shelter Medicine Rotation

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ASCI 51 and Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog. Students must provide documentation of full rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled. See notes in Course Description below.

description: This course is designed to provide Registered Veterinary Technician majors with actual on-the-job experience at an approved work station which is related to classroom instruction. Supervised clinical rotation in a shelter medicine setting. Students will apply foundational veterinary nursing skills such as animal restraint, vaccination protocols, and sanitation procedures in high-volume, fast-paced environments. Emphasis is placed on disease prevention, shelter protocols, and patient safety. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit per AVMA accreditation standards recommendation. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester. Instructor approval required. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by BP & AP 5210 and requirements mandated by American Veterinary Medical Association. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at https://www.mtsac.edu/vettech/immunizations.html. Additional information available at CDC Information (https://www.cdc.gov/rabies/prevention/pre-exposure_vaccinations.html) and AVMA policies (https://www.avma.org/education/center-for-veterinary-accreditation/committee-veterinary-technician-education-activities/cvtea-accreditation-policies-and-procedures-appendix-a)

title: Work Experience in Registered Veterinary Technology - Specialty Rotation

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 90A and ASCI 51 and Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog. Students must provide documentation of full rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled. See notes in Course Description below.

description: This course is designed to provide Registered Veterinary Technician majors with actual on-the-job experience at an approved work station which is related to classroom instruction. Supervised clinical rotation in specialty veterinary practice settings such as dermatology, cardiology, oncology, or equine. Students will develop proficiency in specialty-specific procedures including client intake, chart preparation, and targeted patient care techniques. Emphasis is placed on understanding referral-based workflows and expanding clinical competency in advanced care environments. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit per AVMA accreditation standards recommendation. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester. Instructor approval required. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by BP & AP 5210 and requirements mandated by American Veterinary Medical Association. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at https://www.mtsac.edu/vettech/immunizations.html. Additional information available at CDC Information (https://www.cdc.gov/rabies/prevention/pre-exposure_vaccinations.html) and AVMA policies (https://www.avma.org/education/center-for-veterinary-accreditation/committee-veterinary-technician-education-activities/cvtea-accreditation-policies-and-procedures-appendix-a)

title: Work Experience in Registered Veterinary Technology - Small Animal Rotation

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 60 and AGHE 90B and Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course. Students must provide documentation of full rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled. See notes in Course Description below.

description: Supervised clinical rotation in a small animal hospital setting where students apply veterinary nursing skills, assist with patient care, perform technical procedures, and participate in medical recordkeeping. Emphasis on clinical efficiency, communication, and case management in a real-world veterinary practice. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit per American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) accreditation standards recommendation. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester. Instructor approval required. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by Board Policy (BP) and Administrative Procedure (AP) 5210 and requirements mandated by AVMA. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Additional information available at CDC Information (https://www.cdc.gov/rabies/prevention/pre-exposure_vaccinations.html) and AVMA policies (https://www.avma.org/education/center-for-veterinary-accreditation/committee-veterinary-technician-education-activities/cvtea-accreditation-policies-and-procedures-appendix-a)

title: Work Experience in Registered Veterinary Technology - Emergency Medicine Rotation

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGHE 61 and AGHE 90C and Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course. Students must provide documentation of full rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled. See notes in Course Description below.

description: Supervised clinical rotation in emergency and critical care settings. Students assist with triage, stabilization, inpatient care, and monitoring of hospitalized animals. Emphasis on practical skills, rapid decision-making, and teamwork in high-pressure environments. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit per American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) accreditation standards recommendation. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester. Instructor approval required. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by Board Policy and Administrative Procedure 5210 and requirements mandated by AMVA. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at https://www.mtsac.edu/vettech/immunizations.html. Additional information available at CDC Information (https://www.cdc.gov/rabies/prevention/pre-exposure_vaccinations.html) and AVMA policies (https://www.avma.org/education/center-for-veterinary-accreditation/committee-veterinary-technician-education-activities/cvtea-accreditation-policies-and-procedures-appendix-a)

title: Animal Science
description: A scientific approach to the livestock industry encompassing aspects of animal anatomy, physiology, nutrition, genetics, and epidemiology. Emphasis on the origin, characteristics, adaptations, and contributions of livestock to the modern agriculture industry. Field trips may be required.

title: Animal Nutrition
description: Composition of feeds and their utilization by domestic animals including digestive physiology, animal assessment, feed appraisal and compiling of rations.

title: Animal Nutrition Laboratory
description: Animal nutrition laboratory course emphasizing the composition and analysis of feeds and their utilization by domestic animals, including evaluation of economic trends and current feed industry technology.

title: Exotic Animal Management
description: Care and management of exotic and alternative livestock species with emphasis on identification, health maintenance, handling techniques, nutrition, and reproduction. Includes analysis of industry trends and principal marketing uses of exotic animals.

title: Swine Production
description: Study of the principles and practices in the purebred and commercial pork production industries; emphasis on the importance of breeds, breeding principles, selection, nutrition, environmental management, health, marketing and recordkeeping to ensure scientifically-based management decisions and consumer product acceptance.

title: Horse Production and Management
description: Selection, utilization, and management of the light horse. Emphasis is on evaluation, health care, and handling skills.

title: Sheep Production
description: Survey of the sheep and goat industries; management of commercial, purebred and small farm flocks; selecting, feeding, breeding, and basic care of small ruminants plus marketing of sheep, goats and their products. Laboratory and field trips required.

title: Horse Ranch Management
description: Skills and procedures used in the management of an equine business. Includes business plans and record keeping, staff and financial management, horse care and training, and farm design for a variety of horse operations.

title: Horse Hoof Care
description: Proper horse hoof care; shoeing, trimming, and disease recognition and control.

title: Horse Behavior and Training
description: Breaking and starting young horses. Concentrates on halter training of foals, ground work on yearlings, and green-breaking two-year-olds and up. Includes lunging techniques, driving, and breaking to a saddle. Training in collection, turning, backing, leads, and trailer loading.

title: Beef Production
description: Purebred and commercial beef cattle production; emphasis on the importance of breeds, breeding principles, selection, nutrition, environmental management, health, marketing, and recordkeeping to ensure scientifically based management decisions and consumer product acceptance as applied to beef cattle. Laboratory required. Field trips required.

title: Livestock Judging and Selection
description: Study of form and appearance of farm animals as related to their function. Includes judging of breeding and terminal livestock as well as carcass evaluation. May require field trip.

title: Animal Handling and Restraint
description: Methods of proper handling for large and small animals including chemical and physical techniques of restraint. Field trips required. Note: Students must provide documentation of up-to-date rabies vaccination series or titer prior to being enrolled, as required by BP & AP 5210 and requirements mandated by American Veterinary Medical Association. The cost for two-dose rabies vaccination is approximately $850-$1,050 (prices are subject to change), and both doses are required. Instructions on submitting documentation are available at https://www.mtsac.edu/vettech/immunizations.html . Additional information available at CDC Information and AVMA policies .

title: Work Experience in Agriculture

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.

description: This course is designed to provide Animal Science majors with actual on-the-job experience in an approved work station which is related to classroom instruction. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester. Instructor approval required.

title: Pet Shop Management
description: Pet shop operations and the economic aspects of the pet industry. Organization and operation of pet shops, animal care practices, and sound business management practices.

title: Canine Management
description: Selection, feeding, housing, breeding and management of dogs, including commercial aspects of the dog as a domestic pet. Laboratory work will include practical experience in the handling and training of dogs. May include field trips.

title: Feline Management
description: Care and management of cats including breed identification and characteristics, grooming, showing, nutrition, practical care, behavior, breeding, and housing.

title: Tropical and Coldwater Fish Management
description: Care and keeping of marine and freshwater aquarium fishes, plants, and invertebrates. Guidance on setting up aquariums, choosing compatible species, feeding, health care, breeding, and raising fish.

title: Reptile Management
description: Care and maintenance of reptiles and amphibians, including snakes, lizards, turtles, tortoises, newts, salamanders and frogs. Identification and characteristics of reptiles commonly kept as pets. Housing, feeding, health maintenance, breeding, and raising of reptiles.

title: Aviculture - Cage and Aviary Birds
description: Cage and aviary birds marketed in the wholesale and retail pet trade. Identification, nutrition, breeding, disease prevention and control, and aviary construction. Psittacines, soft bills, finches, game birds, poultry, and ornamental waterfowl.

title: Animal Breeding
description: The science of animal breeding including fundamentals of inheritance, reproduction, and breeding systems for domestic animals. Artificial insemination, embryo manipulation, and current topics in reproductive biotechnology will also be included.

title: Animal Sanitation and Disease Control
description: Prevention and control of infectious diseases affecting domestic animals including basic disease concepts, transmission of infectious diseases, principles of sanitation, and fundamentals of immunology.

title: Animal Sanitation and Disease Control Laboratory

requirements.raw: Corequisite: ASCI 96 (may have been taken previously)

description: Application and development of biosecurity protocols, stressing humane handling and housing, use of disinfectants, and parasite control of domestic animals in the animal sanitation and control lab.

title: Artificial Insemination of Livestock
description: Theory and application of artificial insemination of domestic animals including semen evaluation and processing, heat synchronization, and pregnancy diagnosis.

title: Food Production, Land Use, and Politics - A Global Perspective
description: Surveys the world's food producing systems in terms of economic, political, and cultural forces. Emphasizes ethical, sustainable food producing agriculture.

title: Horticultural Science
description: Horticulture skills and techniques for use in gardening, nursery, and landscape applications. Emphasis on propagation, cultural practices, and the study of plant relationships, structure, growth and development. Off-campus meetings required.

title: Plant Propagation/Greenhouse Management
description: Plant propagation and production practices with emphasis on florists' plants, woody ornamentals, and fruits. Commercial techniques include seed propagation, cuttings, grafting and budding, layering, fern sporing, and division. Stresses greenhouses and other environmental structures for plant propagation and production.

title: Park Facilities
description: Management and operation of different types of park facilities. Includes the management of sports fields, recreation centers, campgrounds, aquatic facilities, and golf courses.

title: Landscape Design
description: Landscape design for residential and small commercial sites including the design process, drafting, graphics, site evaluation, landscaping materials, and plant usage. Field trips and off-campus assignments required.

title: Interior Landscaping
description: Design, installation, and maintenance practices used in interior landscaping. Includes identification, culture, and care of plants suitable for interior use.

title: Integrated Pest Management
description: Common agricultural pests in Southern California and physical, biological, and chemical pest control principles and practices, including integrated pest management (IPM). Stresses use, safety, equipment, laws, and regulations of pesticides. Field trips are required.

title: Ornamental Plants - Herbaceous
description: Identification, growth habits, culture, and ornamental use of landscape annuals, biennials, perennials, ferns, indoor plants, groundcovers, and vines adapted to climates of California. Plants emphasized will come from the Plant California Alliance and National Association of Landscape Professionals (NALP) certification plant lists. Off campus meetings required.

title: Ornamental Plants - Trees and Woody Shrubs
description: Identification, growth habits, culture, and ornamental use of landscape trees and shrubs adapted to climates of California. Plants emphasized will come from the Plant California Alliance and National Association of Landscape Professionals (NALP) certification test plant lists. Off campus meetings required.

title: Landscaping and Nursery Management
description: Operation and management of wholesale and retail nurseries. Includes site location and layout of areas, greenhouse management, soil mixes, proper use of fertilizers, insecticides, fungicides, herbicides, growth regulators, irrigation, mechanization, financing, personnel management, retail displays, advertising, customer relationships, federal, state, and local laws and regulations. Field trips are required.

title: Ornamental Plants California Natives and Southwest Climates
description: Identification, growth habits, culture, and ornamental use of annuals, perennials, groundcovers, shrubs, trees, cacti, and succulents which are native to California and the Southwest, or drought tolerant in Southern California.

title: Turf Grass Production and Management
description: Cultivation, maintenance, and management of turfgrasses utilized for athletic fields, golf courses, parks, cemeteries, and commercial and residential lawns. Identification, installation, cultural requirements, and maintenance practices are emphasized. Field trips required.

title: Sports Turf Management
description: Prepares students to work in the sports turf industry. Emphasizes turf cultural techniques used in sports turf management. Includes turf surfaces used on baseball, football, soccer, tennis, golf courses, driving ranges, and other sports fields in both professional and amateur sports. Field trips required.

title: Soil Science and Management
description: Principles of soil management, including management of air, water, nutrients, organic matter. Study of soil including physical, chemical, and biological properties, classification, derivation, use, function, and management including erosion, moisture retention, structure, cultivation, organic matter, and microbiology as they pertain to optimized plant growth. Laboratory topics include soil type, classification, soil reaction, soil fertility, and physical properties of soil. Laboratory required. Field trips are required.

title: Tractor and Landscape Equipment Operations
description: Selection, operation, repair, and maintenance of power equipment used in the agriculture and landscape industry. Includes two- and four-wheel drive tractors, skip loaders, skid steer loaders, backhoes, lawnmowers, edgers, weed eaters, blower vacuums, rototillers, chainsaws, spraying equipment, and all-terrain vehicles. Laboratory includes use of this equipment.

title: Small Engine Repair I
description: Principles and repair of small engines used in landscape, industrial and agricultural applications. Includes repairs of lawnmowers, chainsaws, 2-cycle engines, 4-cycle engines, spraying equipment, all-terrain vehicles, and other related gas-powered equipment.

title: Irrigation Principles and Design
description: Principles of irrigation, design techniques, sprinkler system components, and hydraulic principles used in nursery management, interior design, residential, and commercial landscapes. Special emphasis is given to water conservation. Field trips are required.

title: Irrigation Systems Management
description: Systematic approach to water conservation in landscapes. Soil-plant-water relationships, evapotranspiration, irrigation schedules, salinity and drainage, and irrigation efficiency. Water measurement, soil moisture measurement, irrigation systems, and practical constraints affecting scheduling. California water supply and budget, water rights, local, state, and federal water institutions, and California water issues. Irrigation efficiency testing will be incorporated to demonstrate proper methods of water audits and system evaluation. Field trips are required.

title: Irrigation - Drip and Low Volume
description: Conservation of water in landscapes by utilization of drip and low-flow irrigation practices. Design, installation techniques, operation, and maintenance of drip and low-flow irrigation systems, including determination of irrigation requirements, selection of emitters and low-flow devices, and uniformity of water distribution. Includes hands-on experience in design and installation techniques. Field trips are required.

title: Construction Fundamentals
description: Construction techniques and tools used in landscaping with construction projects that include surveying techniques, utilities (gas, water, and electricity), woodworking, and masonry.

title: Landscape Hardscape Applications
description: Landscape construction pertaining to hardscape featured in the landscape. Estimation and installation of fences, walks, planters, patios, lighting, barbecues, gazebos, decks, ponds, spas, fountains and pools. Students will gain hands-on experience in the laboratory activities.

title: Landscaping Laws, Contracting, and Estimating
description: Landscape laws, contracting, and estimating as they pertain to landscape construction. Information covered will be helpful for the Landscape Contractor's (C-27 classification) licensing exam administered by the state of California. Off campus assignments required.

title: Urban Arboriculture
description: Care and management of ornamental trees. Includes pruning techniques, fruit tree care, bracing, cabling, and pest control. Safe practices in the use of equipment including the use of ropes, chippers, boom trucks, chain saws, and identification and evaluation of common trees. Prepares students for the tree worker and arborist certification (ISA) exams.

title: Cannabis the Plant and Industry
description: Cannabis the Plant and Industry: This course reviews the origins of the Cannabis genus, its evolution in cultivation, and its cultural impacts leading up to modern industry. Students will become familiar with Cannabis history, laws and regulations, careers, breeding, growth cycles, medicinal applications, and other useful plant characteristics. Students completing this course will demonstrate foundational knowledge useful for entering the Cannabis industry.

title: Cannabis Cultivation
description: This course covers the basics of Cannabis cultivation, including soil media selection, air circulation, tools of the trade, and harvesting. Students will be demonstrate a beginner-level competency in Cannabis cultivation through participation in lectures and lab activities.

title: Cannabis Advanced Cultivation
description: This course covers advanced Cannabis cultivation techniques. In this course, students will learn advanced cultivation techniques, including low-stress and high-stress training, scrogging, defoliation, pinching, fimming, topping, and mainlining. Students will learn how to grow to achieve perpetual harvest, influence THC and Cannabinoid outcomes, improve bud quality, manipulate grow timelines, and advanced lighting techniques.

title: Cannabis Facilities and Operations Management
description: This course reviews the planning, management, and maintenance of Cannabis facilities and operations. In this course, students will learn how to plan grow operations, comply with legal requirements, prepare for compliance inspections, identify trends in the Cannabis industry, and strategically adapt with marketing, sales, and staffing strategies.

title: Work Experience in Cannabis Operations

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AGOR 81 and Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.

description: This course is designed to provide Cannabis majors with actual on-the-job experience at an approved Cannabis work site using skills and knowledge from classroom instruction. A minimum of 108 clock hours per semester is required for each two units of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester.

title: Work Experience in Horticulture

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Three units of any AGOR course, with the exception of AGOR 1 , must be taken prior to or concurrent with AGOR 91 . Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for related program or be concurrently enrolled in a course in such a program.

description: This course is designed to provide majors with actual on-the-job experience at an approved work site using skills and knowledge from classroom instruction. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester.

title: Technical Mathematics in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration
description: Develops mathematical skills required for the study and application of air conditioning and refrigeration, including measurements and equations applied to heat loads, air distribution, electricity, and the design of air conditioning and refrigeration equipment.

title: Welding for Air Conditioning and Refrigeration
description: Fundamentals of welding related to the field of air conditioning and refrigeration with emphasis on the sterile techniques and skills required for joining copper refrigerant lines and the procedures for light fabrication.

title: Air Conditioning Codes and Standards
description: Building codes and standards as they apply to the air conditioning and refrigeration industry. Develops skills necessary to read and interpret building codes and resolve installation and service problems as they apply to the construction industry.

title: Refrigeration Fundamentals
description: Principles of mechanical refrigeration based on the refrigeration cycle and associated mechanical components. Develops skills for interpreting service gauge pressures and sensible temperatures, system dehydration techniques, and the safe handling and containment of refrigerants.

title: Electrical Fundamentals for Air Conditioning and Refrigeration
description: Electrical principles and practices used in air conditioning, refrigeration, and heat pump systems as applied to the development and interpretation of schematics and the sequential approach to wiring circuits including power supplies, motors, and controls. Develops skills for designing electrical circuits, and electrical trouble shooting.

title: Gas Heating Fundamentals
description: Theory, operation, and application of natural gas and propane heating systems used in residential and light commercial heating installations, including the properties of fuel gasses, gas combustion, furnace construction, pilot proving devices, and ignition systems.

title: Heat Load Calculations and Design
description: Heat loss and heat gain will be examined, developed, and applied to residential dwellings air conditioning systems. Equipment sizing, selection, and duct design based on the Heat Load of the structure. Heat Load calculation software will be explored and used to aid in the process.

title: Commercial Electrical for Air Conditioning and Refrigeration
description: Electrical control of commercial air conditioning and refrigeration equipment emphasizing time clocks, defrost, three phase transformers, three phase motors, Variable Frequency Drives, and troubleshooting of three phase systems.

title: Air Properties and Measurement
description: Investigates the air-side operating theory and application of comfort cooling systems. This course will broaden the student's understanding of air conditioning systems by addressing psychrometrics to include the measurement of dry bulb and wet bulb temperatures, relative humidity, dew point temperatures, and sensible and latent heat processes.

title: Commercial Systems
description: This course is designed for the advanced student to gain familiarity with commercial systems, which are not limited to air handlers, cooling towers, water pumps, chillers, and thermal storage. Students will also increase their understanding of how large complex buildings are to be conditioned.

title: Commercial Refrigeration

requirements.raw: Advisory: AIRC 10 and AIRC 11 and AIRC 20 and AIRC 31

description: Commercial refrigeration systems for medium and low temperature applications. Covers applications for the pressure-enthalpy diagram, oil control and safeties, temperature and relative humidity control, head pressure control systems, defrost methods, compressor protections, and component selection. Refrigerant safety, handling, and storage methods are emphasized.

title: Supermarket Refrigeration Systems
description: Medium and low temperature multiplexed supermarket refrigeration systems that use hydrofluorocarbons (HFC) refrigerants. Explores the mechanical operation of multiplexed compressors based on refrigeration demand and the mechanical components required that include compressors, head pressure control devices, high and low side oil control systems, defrost systems, pressure regulators, subcoolers, and heat recovery systems. Field trips required.

title: Transcritical CO2 Refrigeration Systems
description: Transcritical supermarket refrigeration systems using carbon dioxide (CO2) as the refrigerant. Includes CO2 cascade systems, hybrid cascade systems, pumped secondary CO2 systems, and transcritical booster CO2 Systems. Explores the difference between subcritical and transcritical operating conditions and the supporting components. Emphasis on safety handling procedures of CO2 as a refrigerant. Field trips required.

title: Building Automation Fundamentals

requirements.raw: Advisory: AIRC 20 and AIRC 25 and AIRC 31 and AIRC 34

description: Basics of commercial heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) control theory as it applies to control systems. Building automation systems (BAS) controller wiring for power, communication, inputs, and outputs. Navigating the computer operating system environment, BAS software, and applications. Word processing, spreadsheets, and flow-charts for use with BAS systems.

title: Building Automation Networks and Programming
description: Programming heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) direct digital controllers using line (text) programming, icon based programming, and block programming. Stresses good programming practices including complete program documentation.

title: Energy Management

requirements.raw: Advisory: AIRC 31 and AIRC 34 and AIRC 61 and AIRC 65

description: Principles and practical applications for energy cost reduction and strategies. Emphasis on the use of Building Automation Systems to achieve control over energy costs. Includes theory for sustainable Green Building Technologies with introduction to Energy Star buildings and Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) programs.

title: Work Experience in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course.

description: Supervised work experience in air conditioning and refrigeration at an approved work site with related classroom instruction. This work experience may be during a regular semester or during a summer session. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester is required for each one unit of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week are equally distributed throughout the semester. Instructor approval required.

title: Aircraft Powerplant Theory

requirements.raw: Corequisite: AIRM 70A (May have been taken previously)

description: Theory and overhaul of aircraft reciprocating and turbine powerplants. Approved and required for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) powerplant certification.

title: Aircraft Powerplant Systems
description: Reciprocating and turbine engine systems and components. Approved and required for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) powerplant certification.

title: Aircraft Airframe Maintenance Structures
description: This course is approved by the Federal Aviation Administration and meets requirements for all Aircraft Powerplant and Airframe Maintenance Technology majors. Structure topics span nomenclature and aerodynamics, set back and bend allowance, riveting, wood, fabric, paint, repairing aluminum, plastics, composites, rigging, component overhaul and inspection.

title: Aircraft Airframe Maintenance Systems
description: Airframe systems in hydraulics, landing gear, pneumatics, pressurization, instruments, fuel, fire, communication, navigation, autopilots, and RADAR. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

title: Aircraft Maintenance Electricity and Electronics
description: Electrical theory, series and parallel circuits, batteries, and electrical measuring instruments. Required for Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certification.

title: Aircraft Maintenance Electricity and Electronics
description: Principles of alternating current electricity with emphasis on components and circuits. Required for Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certification.

title: Aviation Maintenance Science
description: Federal aviation regulations, interpretation of aircraft drawings, basic physics, technical mathematics, and aircraft weight and balance computations. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved course required of all aircraft powerplant and airframe maintenance technology majors.

title: Aircraft Materials and Processes
description: Part 147 Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved course covering aviation materials, non-destructive testing, basic heat-treating and machining.

title: Aircraft Maintenance Technology - Work Experience

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog

description: Combines aircraft maintenance experience in addition to classroom instruction for college credit. Two units of credit will be earned as a result of 108 work hours. The employer and evaluator will have the student perform aircraft maintenance work under direct supervision at a maintenance facility.

title: Laboratory Studies in Aircraft Maintenance Technology
description: Additional lab instruction for students lacking Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) mandated projects to complete a training certificate, required remediation of program modules, or laboratory assignments.

title: Airframe Theory

requirements.raw: Advisory: AIRM 70A or AIRM 70B or AIRM 71 or AIRM 72

description: A Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved course covering aircraft flight, flight control, and construction methods and procedures.

title: Airframe Wood, Fabric, and Paint
description: Aircraft structural designs, wood structures, fabric covering, and aircraft finishes. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and required for the Airframe and Aircraft Powerplant Maintenance Technology major.

title: Airframe Aluminum Repair and Plastics
description: Aircraft structural repair of aluminum and aircraft plastics. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and required for the Airframe and Aircraft Powerplant Maintenance Technology major.

title: Airframe Composites, Rigging, and Inspection

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AIRM 90A and AIRM 90B and AIRM 91A

description: Composite materials used in aircraft construction, rigging, and inspection. Approved by the Federal Aviation Association (FAA) and required for the Airframe and Aircraft Powerplant Maintenance Technology major.

title: Airframe Hydraulics and Pneumatics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AIRM 90A and AIRM 90B and AIRM 91A and AIRM 91B

description: Aircraft hydraulic and pneumatic power systems, landing gear, and wheel and brake systems. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and required for the Airframe and Aircraft Powerplant Maintenance Technology major.

title: Airframe Fuel and Environmental Systems
description: Aircraft environmental systems, instrument systems, and fuel systems. Approved by the Federal Aviation Association (FAA) and required for the Aircraft Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance Technology major.

title: Airframe Warning and Fire Systems
description: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved course covering aircraft cabin heating and cooling, communication and navigation systems, and ice and rain control systems in small and large aircraft.

title: Aircraft Communication, Navigation, Radar, and Autopilot Systems

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AIRM 92A and AIRM 92B and AIRM 93A

description: Aircraft navigation and communication systems, radar systems, and autopilot systems. Course approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and required for the Airframe and Aircraft Powerplant Maintenance Technology major.

title: Aircraft Powerplant Theory

requirements.raw: Advisory: AIRM 70A and AIRM 70B and AIRM 71 and AIRM 72

description: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved course covering piston powerplant theory. Includes calculations and construction methods.

title: Aircraft Powerplant Inspection and Maintenance
description: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved course covering piston engine overhaul, inspection, and troubleshooting procedures.

title: Aircraft Turbine Engines
description: Aircraft turbine engine history, construction, thrust formulas and turbine engine types. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and required for the Airframe and Aircraft Powerplant Maintenance Technology Major. Required for FAA certification.

title: Aircraft Propellers

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AIRM 95A and AIRM 95B and AIRM 96A

description: Propeller theory, nomenclature, application, constant speed devices, and propeller controls. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and required for the Airframe and Aircraft Powerplant Maintenance Technology Major. Required for FAA certification.

title: Aircraft Powerplant Instrumentation

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AIRM 95A and AIRM 95B and AIRM 96A and AIRM 96B

description: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved course covering instrumentation, fire and smoke detection, and fire suppression systems used in small and large aircraft.

title: Aircraft Powerplant Fuel Systems
description: Reciprocating engine and turbine engine fuels, fuel metering devices, and system operation. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

title: Aircraft Power Plant Ignition Systems
description: Reciprocating and turbine engine ignition system theory and maintenance. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

title: Aircraft Powerplant Lubricating Systems

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: AIRM 97A and AIRM 97B and AIRM 98A

description: Reciprocating and turbine engine lubricants and lubricating systems. Approved by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Required for FAA certification.

title: Aircraft Recognition and Performance
description: Designed for students who want to become air traffic controllers for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Students will learn to recognize the distinctive features of aircraft, identify types of aircraft, classify aircraft as to FAA category and class, and analyze aircraft for performance characteristics required for air traffic control separation. Commercial Pilot majors are encouraged to take the class as an elective course.

title: Terminal Air Traffic Control
description: Designed for students who want to become air traffic controllers for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Students will learn about aircraft operation in the National Airspace System, control tower operations, terminal radar control, radio communication techniques and phraseology, and responding to emergencies.

title: Air Traffic Control Laboratory
description: Concepts, procedures, and skills related to air traffic control. Microphone technique, voice control, phraseology, facility and interfacility coordination, strip markings, airport traffic control, weather observing, and control tower functions.

title: Enroute Air Traffic Control
description: Enroute air traffic control operations in the National Airspace System. Includes radar and non-radar separation rules, enroute air traffic control clearances, emergencies and search and rescue, and future air traffic control technologies. This course is designed for students who want to become air traffic controllers for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

title: Enroute Radar Laboratory
description: Simulation of an air traffic control radar facility concentrating on air route traffic control, and approach and departure procedures using appropriate phraseology, flight progress strip markings and radar separation standards.

title: Air Traffic Control Team Skills
description: Leadership skills for aviation professionals, with emphasis on FAA Crew Resource Management. This course will introduce students to the skills required to work in an aviation group environment. Students will be able to identify personality types and temperaments, analyze skills necessary to manage and improve individual performance, work effectively in the team environment, and recognize human factors that affect air traffic control, identify "threat and error" countermeasures.

title: College Composition for Non-Native English Speakers

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ENGL 68 or AMLA 90 or appropriate placement

description: Engages non-native English students in the reading and writing process with emphasis on college-level reading, critical analysis, research skills, and expository and argumentative composition mindful of purpose and audience while developing an awareness of fundamental principles of cultural competence and linguistic awareness that are inherent in language learning.

title: Basic to Intermediate Writing and Reading

requirements.raw: Advisory: Guided self-placement tool or completion of noncredit ESL Level 4

description: Basic to intermediate level accelerated writing and reading for non-native speakers with an emphasis on preparation for academic writing, critical thinking, and vocabulary development.

title: American Language Basic Reading
description: Basic reading and vocabulary for non-native English speakers.

title: American English Pronunciation
description: Pronunciation for English language learners with emphasis on analysis of individual strengths and weaknesses. Focus on improving articulation, stress, intonation patterns, and listening.

title: Intermediate to Advanced Writing and Reading
description: Intermediate to advanced accelerated writing and reading for English Language Learners with an emphasis on preparation for academic writing, critical thinking, and vocabulary development.

title: American Language Intermediate Reading

requirements.raw: Advisory: Eligibility for AMLA 80 or ESL LVL5 or ESL LVL6

description: Intermediate reading and vocabulary for English language learners.

title: American Language Conversational English
description: Enhances ability of English Language Learners to communicate in personal and academic situations. Emphasis on clear and sophisticated expression of ideas as well as increasing confidence in communication.

title: Idiomatic English
description: Intermediate course in the study of idiomatic language, including common American idioms and proverbs, as used in everyday language situations.

title: AMLA Grammar Foundations for English Language Learners
description: Focuses on beginning to intermediate grammar topics for the academic success of English language learners, with an emphasis on usage that improves writing and speaking. Topics covered include most frequently used verb forms and tenses, sentence parts, sentence types and sentence structure, as well as the writing process and editing skills in writing.

title: College Preparation Writing for English Language Learners
description: Introduce advanced English Language Learners to academic reading, writing, and communicating while nurturing reflection and critical thinking skills for engaging in college-level course work. Students complete writing assignments based on readings in different genres, utilize synthesized information from on a variety of class sources, and establish a formal writing style in academic English in preparation for college-level writing

title: American Language Advanced Reading for English Language Learners
description: Advanced reading and vocabulary for English Language Learners, with special attention to strategies that increase comprehension, vocabulary development, and critical thinking

title: American Language Formal Speaking
description: Enhances the ability of English Language Learners to listen effectively and speak formally. Emphasis is on note taking, outlining, organizing speeches, and verbal articulation of ideas.

title: American Language Colloquial English for English Language Learners
description: Advanced course in the study of colloquial English, including common American idioms and proverbs, slang, professionalisms, body language, language-appropriate communication, online English, and jargon, as used in everyday language situations to understand American intelligibility in a variety of informal settings.

title: AMLA Advanced Grammar for English Language Learners
description: Focus on advanced grammar topics for English Language Learners, with an emphasis on constructions that improve writing and speaking. Topics covered will include level of diction, importance of word choice, sentence sophistication, sentence connectors, sentence variety, verb tense review, modals, verbals, passive voice, and coherence devices.

title: American Culture for English Language Learners

requirements.raw: Advisory: AMLA 90 (May have been taken previously)

description: Introduction to various aspects of American culture, including beliefs, lifestyles, attitudes, values, college culture, and issues for English Language Learners. This course is designed to promote a better understanding and awareness of American culture to help students not only succeed in college but to integrate into society and add to the fabric of the community. The course contextualizes social, political, religious, intellectual, technological, and economic facets of the prism of American life.

title: Introductory Human Anatomy
description: Macroscopic and microscopic structures of the human body. Emphasis on gross and microscopic structure of the integumentary, skeletal, muscular, nervous, sensory, endocrine, cardiovascular, lymphatic, respiratory, digestive, excretory and reproductive systems from cellular to organ system levels of organization. Comparison of normal, aging, and diseased structures. This course is primarily intended for nursing, allied health careers such as respiratory technician and radiology technology, kinesiology, and other health related majors.

title: Introductory Human Physiology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( CHEM 10 or CHEM 40 or CHEM 50 or CHEM 50H ) and ( ANAT 10A or ANAT 35 )

description: Study of the physiological principles, function, integration and homeostasis of the human body at the cellular, tissue, organ, organ system and organism level: integumentary system, bone, nervous system, skeletal muscle, smooth muscle, cardiac muscle, sensory organs, cardiovascular system, lymphatic and immune systems, respiratory system, urinary system, digestive system, endocrine system, reproductive system, and electrolyte and acid-base balance. This course is primarily intended for Nursing, Allied Health, Kinesiology and other health related majors.

title: Human Anatomy

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: BIOL 1 or BIOL 4 or BIOL 4H

description: Study of the anatomy of the human body. The development, structure and components of organ systems of the body will be studied at the gross and histological levels. Laboratory study will include the use of human anatomical models and human skeletons as well as the observation of prosected human cadavers and prepared histology slides.

title: Human Physiology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( BIOL 1 or BIOL 4 or BIOL 4H ) and ANAT 35 and ( CHEM 10 or CHEM 40 )

description: Human physiology at the cellular and molecular levels covering muscular, nervous, circulatory, respiratory, renal, digestive, endocrine, and reproductive systems. Includes regulation and integration of organ systems where appropriate.

title: Pathophysiology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ANAT 10B or ANAT 36 ) and ( MICR 1 or MICR 22 )

description: Alterations in homeostasis and cellular function and diseases of bodily systems. Emphasis is placed on a comparison between disease states and structure and function in healthy individuals.

title: Human Prosection

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ANAT 35 and Instructor approval required
