Design and configuration of remote cloud access, Cyber, and Virtual Private Network (VPN) security, local area networks (LAN), wide area networks (WAN), Virtual LANs (VLAN), Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), advanced Subnetting and Supernetting, command line Interface (CLI), Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol version 4 and 6 (IPv4 and IPv6), advanced switching, virtual LAN (VLAN) and InterVLAN routing, access control lists (ACL), wireless security, dynamic and static routing, network architecture, controller-based network automation, and security services. Student must be enrolled in CISN 51L , a concurrent lab co-requisite.

title: Cisco CCNA Networking and Routing Laboratory
description: Lab to prepare for Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) certification and industry network security implementation. Design and configuration of remote cloud access, Cyber, and Virtual Private Network (VPN) security, local area networks (LAN), wide area networks (WAN), Virtual LANs (VLAN), Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), advanced Subnetting and Supernetting, command line Interface (CLI), Transmission Control Protocol and Internet Protocol version 4 and 6 (IPv4 and IPv6), advanced switching, virtual LAN (VLAN) and InterVLAN routing, access control lists (ACL), wireless security, dynamic and static routing, network architecture, controller-based network automation, and security services. Student must be enrolled in CISN 51 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Introduction to Cloud Computing
description: Concepts and principles of cloud computing that shift information systems from on-premises computing infrastructure to highly scalable internet architectures. Topics includes cloud computing technologies, cloud services (storage, servers and software applications), cloud providers, industry cloud practices, cloud careers, and industry demand for cloud skills. Students analyze a variety of case studies to effectively evaluate and assess the business and technical benefits of cloud computing and cloud applications.

title: Cloud Computing Database Essentials
description: Concepts and skills in planning, designing, and using different cloud database data storage solutions; define, operate and scale both Structured Query Language (SQL) and Not only SQL (NoSOL) data storage solutions; using Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) and SQL to create and fill tables, retrieve and manipulate data; using object-based Application Programming Interface (APIs) to serialize objects to Amazon DynamoDB for NoSQL solutions and other topics like automated backups, transaction logs, restoration, and retention.

title: Compute Engines in Cloud Computing
description: Concepts and skills on building cloud computing systems using a common set of core technologies, algorithms, and design principles centered around distributed systems; using Amazon Web Services (AWS) Management Console to provision, load-balance, and scale applications with compute engines like Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) and the AWS Elastic Beanstalk (EB); and rationale for using AWS and design principles of scalable cloud applications.

title: Security in Amazon Web Services
description: Concepts and skills on protecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability of computing systems and data; how Cloud providers use redundant and layered controls, continuous validation and testing, and a substantial amount of automation to ensure the underlying infrastructure is continuously monitored and protected; Shared Responsibility Model; and identifying through the Cloud Management Console the security tools and features provided by the Cloud platform.

Concurrent enrollment in the lecture course CISP 21 - Programming in Java is required.

title: Advanced Java Programming
description: Advanced object-oriented programming using Java: designing, coding, testing, and implementing multi-tier applications in serialization, multithreading, Advanced Swing Components (ASC), networking, server-side technology which include servlets, remote method invocation (RMI), Java server pages, Java Database Connectivity (JDBC), public key infrastructure (PKI), mobile applications, and security. Student must be enrolled in CISP 24L , a concurrent lab co-requisite.

title: Advanced Java Laboratory
description: Laboratory for advanced programming concepts using Java: designing, coding, testing, and implementing multi-tier applications in serialization, multithreading, Advanced Swing Components (ASC), networking, server-side technology which include servlets, remote method invocation (RMI), Java server pages, Java Database Connectivity (JDBC), public key infrastructure (PKI), mobile applications, and security. Student must be enrolled in CISP 24 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Programming in C++

description: Object-oriented programming in C++ including object-oriented design, documentation, and debugging techniques. title: Programming in C++ Laboratory
description: Laboratory for object-oriented programming in C++ including object-oriented design, documentation, and debugging techniques. Elementary control structures, classes, overload operators and functions, and single and multiple inheritance. Student must be enrolled in CISP 31 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Advanced C++ Programming
description: Object-oriented programming in C++ concepts and principles. Covers data structures: vectors, linked lists, queues, stacks and hash tables, graphical-user interface (GUI), database access, and web services. Students must be enrolled in CISP 34L , a concurrent lab co-requisite.

title: Advanced C++ Programming Laboratory
description: Laboratory for object-oriented programming in C++ concepts. Students must be enrolled in CISP 34 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

description: Laboratory for CISP 41 - C# Programming exercises focusing on design and development of object-oriented business programs and applications, documentation and debugging techniques, user-interface, objects, variables, methods, events, elementary control structures, lists, arrays, and inheritance. title: Advanced Programming in Python
description: Advanced object-oriented programming using Python. Topics include: data structures and algorithms; JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) processing; threads and concurrency; web scraping; web applications; scalable applications on the Amazon web services (AWS) cloud; web services interaction; operating systems interaction; and real world tasks automation. Student must enroll in CISP 74 L concurrently.

title: Advanced Programming in Python Laboratory
description: Laboratory for advanced object-oriented programming using Python. Student must be enrolled in CISP 74 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Practical Computer Security
description: Computer security for all computer users. Provides awareness for computer users to protect user accounts and computer systems from attacks. Projects illustrate security software and hardware configuration.

title: Principles of Information Systems Security
description: Systems Security Certified Practitioner (SSCP) course preparation including practical technical skills for operational information technology (IT) roles.

title: Operating Systems Security
description: Operating systems security concepts and techniques: covers how attackers operate, how viruses strike, strengthening operating systems, repelling attacks, and applying security techniques to different operating systems like Windows, Unix, Linux, etc.

title: Network Vulnerabilities and Countermeasures
description: Network vulnerabilities from a hacker's perspective. Cyber security legal and ethical issues. Written security, use policy, and instance response policy. Scanning and penetration tests, vulnerability assessments, and countermeasures for Windows and Linux operating systems. Secure programming, virtual private network (VPN), cryptography, wireless, Web, and remote access securities. Student must be enrolled in CISS 21L , a concurrent lab co-requisite.

title: Network Vulnerabilities and Countermeasures Laboratory
description: Laboratory for network vulnerabilities from a hacker's perspective. Cyber security legal and ethical issues. Written security, use policy, and instance response policy. Scanning and penetration tests, vulnerability assessments and countermeasures for Windows and Linux operating systems. Secure programming, virtual private network (VPN), cryptography, wireless, Web, and remote access securities. Student must be enrolled in CISS 21 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Cyber, Cloud Network Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS)
description: Computer forensic, Penetration (PEN) testing, and packet crafting tools to monitor, troubleshoot, identify threads and traffic from Cyber, Cloud, and local networks. Configure, deploy, detect, and block attacks using Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance IDS/IPS, Windows Snort IDS/IPS, and open-source IDS/IPS including Linux Snort, OSSEC, and Security Onion (Snort/Suricata). Student must be enrolled in CISS 23L , a concurrent lab co-requisite.

title: Cyber, Cloud Network Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) Laboratory
description: Laboratory course for computer forensic, Penetration (PEN) testing, and packet crafting tools to monitor, troubleshoot, identify threads and traffic from Cyber, Cloud, and local networks. Configure, deploy, detect, and block attacks using Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance IDS/IPS, Windows Snort IDS/IPS, and open-source IDS/IPS including Linux Snort, OSSEC, and Security Onion (Snort/Suricata). Student must be enrolled in CISS 23 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Cyber, Cloud Network Security and Firewalls
description: Design, configure, deploy, and maintain Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA), Windows, and Linux firewalls to secure Cyber, Cloud, and local networks. Topics include IPsec and TLS Virtual Private Network (VPN) remote clients, Access Control Lists (ACL), Confidentiality Integrity Availability (CIA), Radius, and Certificate Authentication (CA). Student must enroll in CISS 25L concurrently.

title: Cyber, Cloud Network Security and Firewalls Laboratory
description: Laboratory course to design, configure, deploy, and maintain Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA), Windows, and Linux firewalls to secure Cyber, Cloud, and local networks. Topics include IPsec and TLS Virtual Private Network (VPN) remote clients, Access Control Lists (ACL), Confidentiality Integrity Availability (CIA), Radius, and Certificate Authentication (CA). Student must enroll in CISS 25L concurrently.

title: Cyber Defense
description: Cyber security hands-on activities in defending, responding, mitigating, and analyzing attacks through IT infrastructure and application service vulnerabilities. Prepare students to secure, configure, monitor, and analyze computer, switch, router, firewall, Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS), Voice over IP (VoIP), smart phone, and application services such as Web, email, Structured Query Language (SQL) database, Domain Name Systems (DNS), and Virtual Private Network (VPN).

title: CNASM Service Learning
description: Explore career objectives and advanced skills from Computer Network Administration and Security Management (CNASM) courses through lab activities and community services.

title: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript Programming
description: Plan, program, implement, publish, and maintain web sites using Hypertext Markup Language version 5 (HTML5), Cascading Style Sheets version 3 (CSS3), and JavaScript. Includes working with text, semantic, and multimedia objects, tables, forms, Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), Document Object Model (DOM), cross-browser compatibility, markup validation, client-side interactivity, and principles of web page design, web site construction, documentation, and publishing.

title: Secure Web Server Programming in Python
description: Secure web programming to create user interfaces, extract information and manage databases, manage files, format reports, and access web servers using Python programming language. Student must be enrolled in CISW 24L , a concurrent lab co-requisite.

title: Secure Web Server Programming in Python Laboratory
description: Laboratory for secure web programming to create user interfaces, extract information and manage databases, manage files, format reports, and access web servers using Python programming language. Student must be enrolled in CISW 24 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Secure Web Server Programming in PHP Laboratory
description: Laboratory to plan, install, and manage secure Apache Web servers using server side programming language like PHP (PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor) to access, manage, and secure MySQL databases. Student must be enrolled in CISW 31 , a concurrent lecture co-requisite.

title: Fundamentals of Computer Science

requirements.raw: Advisory: Eligibility for ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Computer hardware and software. General computer organization and information representation. Binary and hexadecimal number systems. Algorithm design and problem-solving techniques. Introduction to programming using a high level language such as C++, Java, or Python.

title: C++ Language and Object Development
description: For computer science, mathematics, engineering and other science students. C++ programming and object-oriented paradigm. Control structures, functions, arrays, pointers and strings, classes and data abstraction, C++ object programming, operator overloading, inheritance, virtual functions and polymorphism, stream input and output, templates, exception handling, file processing. Data structures in C++, string processing and recursion.

title: Java Language and Object Oriented Programming
description: Java language and object-oriented programming (OOP) with Java as well as general concepts and techniques of computer programming. Topics include: Java expressions, flow control, methods and program structure, Java classes, overloading, object references, inheritance, Java library packages, exceptions, file input/output (I/O), graphical user interface (GUI), and event handling. A course for computer science, engineering, mathematics, and other science students.

title: Assembly Language/Machine Architecture
description: Organization and operation of real computer systems at the assembly language level using the Intel x86, x86-64, or ARM family of processors; mapping statements and constructs in a high-level language onto sequences of machine instructions; internal representations of simple data types and structures; numerical computation, noting various data representation errors and potential procedural errors; investigation of basic principles of operating systems; and programming language translation process.

title: Discrete Mathematics Applied to Computer Science

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: CSCI 110 and MATH 130 or MATH 150 or MATH 160 or MATH 180

description: A study of set theory, propositional and predicate calculus, modular arithmetic, counting techniques, combinatorics, mathematical induction, recursion, binary search trees, graphs, and finite probability. For students in computer science, engineering, mathematics and other sciences.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Abstract data types and algorithm analysis and design. Linear data structures including stacks, queues, vectors, and lists. Non-linear data structures including trees, binary search trees, heaps, priority queues, and graphs. Searching, sorting, and hash tables. Design patterns including divide-and-conquer, greedy method, and dynamic programming. Memory and disk management techniques.

title: Building Information Modeling for Construction
description: Building Information Modeling (BIM) principles for construction management, and understanding coordination of building elements, building engineering systems, infrastructure systems, clash detection, construction cost estimating and scheduling. Field trips may be required.

title: Construction Planning and Management
description: Project construction principles: preconstruction services, estimating and bidding, construction scheduling concepts, and a virtual construction environment of the preconstruction phase. Field trips may be required.

title: Construction Controls
description: Construction business principles: budget and cost forecasting and scheduling, regulations and legal requirements for construction, and how to manage the closeout process the construction phase. Field trips may be required.

title: Construction Operations
description: Project construction principles: detail scheduling and forecasting, means and methods for construction, and how to use Building Information Modeling (BIM) and virtual coordination during the construction phase. Field trips may be required.

title: Construction Management Work Experience

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: CMGT 121 and CMGT 130 and CMGT 140 and CMGT 150 and Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.

description: This course is designed to provide actual on-the-job experience in in the construction management profession at an approved work site which is related to classroom instruction. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester of supervised work is required for each unit of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week be equally distributed throughout the semester. This course is available to students achieving a minimum of 12 units in construction management. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Introduction to College
description: Higher education and the college experience including orientation to college and higher education resources. Explores degree and transfer requirements, factors in educational decision-making, educational planning.

title: Introduction to College - Honors
description: Higher education and the college experience including orientation to college and resources. Explores degree and transfer requirements, factors in educational decision-making, and educational planning. May not receive credit for both COUN 1 and COUN 1H .

title: College Success Strategies
description: Strategies and techniques to be a successful college student including self-management, study habits, campus resources, career exploration and educational planning. Develop skills necessary to reach educational and career goals.

title: Career and Life Planning
description: A systematic approach to self-exploration related to the career and life planning process, including identification of values, interests, skills, personality and self-management style. Develop decision making and goal setting skills and identify barriers to success. Explores and evaluates careers and job search techniques.

title: Planning for Transfer Success

requirements.raw: Advisory: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Analysis and exploration of the university transfer process with particular emphasis on the systems of higher education in California (CSU, UC, and independent colleges and universities) as well as Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU) and schools with designations such Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSI), and Asian American and Native American, and Pacific Islander-Serving Institutions (AANAPISI). Students will be able to analyze the transfer pathway through the application of theory and concepts relevant to the transfer student experience. Financial aid resources, scholarships, and transfer preparation and transition programs will be explored to assist students in making informed decisions related to transfer with particular emphasis on specialized student support programs and resources for historically underrepresented students such as, but not limited to, undocumented students, students with disabilities, foster youth, students with dependents and LGBTQ+ students. Off-campus tour required.

title: Planning for Transfer Success - Honors

requirements.raw: Advisory: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Honors course analyzing and exploring the university transfer process with particular emphasis on the systems of higher education in California (CSU, UC and independent colleges and universities) as well as Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU) and schools with designations such Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSI), and Asian American and Native American, and Pacific Islander-Serving Institutions (AANAPISI). Students will be able to analyze the transfer pathway through the application of theory and concepts relevant to the transfer student experience. Financial aid resources, scholarships, and transfer preparation and transition programs will be explored to assist students in making informed decisions related to transfer with particular emphasis on specialized student support programs and resources for historically underrepresented students such as, but not limited to, undocumented students, students with disabilities, foster youth, students with dependents and LGBTQ+ students. Off-campus tour required. An honors course designed to provide an enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both COUN 7 and COUN 7H .

title: Education for Critical Consciousness

requirements.raw: Advisory: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Through a Counseling discipline lens, this course will provide an overview of the history and structure of higher education in the U.S. It will critically analyze the educational experience of diverse students as well as their social identities and factors that contribute to their college success, using a student development theoretical framework. Accordingly, this course will foster important dialogue reframing and reimagining higher education in the U.S. It will promote personal agency and empowerment to improve the achievement gap of historically underrepresented students. Relevant legislation and contemporary issues in higher education will be examined.

title: Introduction to Peer Mentoring
description: Group experience with interpersonal communication and approaches to student to student peer mentoring. Provide opportunities to develop skills with a variety of communication styles that include open expression, active listening, and feedback.

title: Introduction to Career Exploration
description: Introductory career planning course designed for students who want assistance in making informed career decisions. A variety of assessments, inventories, and computer generated information will be used to help students explore careers and majors.

title: Student Success for Single Parents
description: Identify behavior patterns that influence student success. Develop skills and strategies to be a successful single parent college student. Topics include communication, assertiveness, conflict resolution, goal setting, decision making, time management, educational planning, career assessment, college resources, self-advocacy, and building a strong support system.

title: Culinary Work Experience

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.

description: Provides students with actual on-the-job experience in an approved culinary worksite that is related to classroom-based learning. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester of supervised work is required for each unit of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week be equally distributed throughout the semester. Work experience placement is not guaranteed, but assistance is provided by faculty.

title: Professional Cooking Foundations
description: This lecture-based course provides a comprehensive introduction to the principles and practices of professional cooking. Students will explore core culinary techniques, kitchen terminology, ingredient functions, and the structure of professional kitchens. Emphasis is placed on understanding cooking methods, flavor development, menu planning, and food safety. The course also includes an overview of career pathways in the culinary field and develops essential soft skills such as communication, time management, teamwork, and professional conduct. Designed for aspiring culinary professionals, this course lays the theoretical groundwork for success in kitchen environments or further hands-on training.

title: Professional Cooking I

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: HRM 52 and students are required to present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: Introduces professional kitchen operations through a comprehensive blend of lecture and hands-on lab instruction. Topics include food safety and sanitation, teamwork, tools and equipment, knife skills, mise en place, menu development, and core cooking methods. Students will explore the principles of flavor development and apply techniques to a variety of ingredients, including stocks, sauces, vegetables, grains, proteins, and seafood. In the lab, students will practice mise en place by organizing and preparing ingredients and tools before executing and presenting a variety of dishes. Each session emphasizes proper technique, efficient workflow, and clean presentation. Techniques covered include simmering, sauteing, roasting, braising, grilling, poaching, frying, and fabricating poultry. Students will also develop their understanding of classical knife cuts, emulsified dressings, and foundational preparations such as soups, salads, and sandwiches. Students are required to present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification and must wear the appropriate professional uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Hospitality, Culinary Arts or Baking or Pastry.

title: Professional Cooking II

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: HRM 52 and CUL 102 . Students are required to present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry. This intensive, hands-on course propels experienced culinary students beyond recipes. Through direct engagement with premium ingredients and diverse cooking methods, one will cultivate an intuitive understanding of flavor development and product outcomes. Sharpen skills in a dynamic environment focused on cooking, tasting, and critical evaluation. Valid Food Safety Manager Certification and full professional kitchen uniform, including non-slip footwear. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: Garde Manger

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: HRM 52 and Students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: Embark on a culinary journey into the fascinating world of the Garde Manger, the cold kitchen, essential to any professional culinary operation. This foundational course will equip students with the fundamental techniques and knowledge required to excel in the preparation and presentation of a diverse range of cold dishes. Through hands-on practice and theoretical exploration, students will master essential skills in charcuterie, pates and terrines, salads and dressings, canapes and hors d'oeuvres, cheese and fruit platters, and buffet presentation. Emphasis will be placed on food safety, sanitation, proper knife skills, flavor development, and creative plating. Students are required to present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification and must wear the appropriate professional uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: Baking and Pastry I

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: To participate in this course, students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry. Feed your passion for the sweet side of the culinary arts! Take a journey into the foundational world of baking and pastry! This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the essential techniques, principles, and ingredients that form the bedrock of successful baking. Through hands-on practice and engaging instruction, students will learn fundamental mixing methods, understand the role of key ingredients, and develop the skills to create a variety of classic baked goods and pastries. Emphasis will be placed on accuracy, consistency, and developing a strong understanding of basic formulas. Students are required to present a valid Food Handler Certificate and must wear the appropriate uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear. This course is intended for students interested in commercial application in restaurants, bakeries, and other food service facilities. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: Baking and Pastry II

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: CUL 105 and students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: Theory and principles of fine baking, pastry, and desserts with emphasis on the European tradition. Students will create and decorate cakes, fine pastry, chocolate work, and classic and modern desserts Delve deeper into the intricate theory and refined principles of fine baking, pastry, and dessert artistry, with a distinct focus on the esteemed European tradition. Building upon foundational skills, this intensive Level II course challenges students to master advanced techniques in creating both classic and contemporary desserts. Emphasis will be placed on cultivating exceptional organizational skills, maximizing speed and efficiency in production, and achieving stunning professional presentation. Designed for aspiring professionals, this course provides the advanced knowledge and practical expertise essential for success in demanding commercial environments such as fine-dining restaurants, upscale bakeries, and other high-end food service establishments. Students are required to present a valid Food Handler Certificate and must wear the appropriate professional uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts, or Baking and Pastry.

title: World Cuisines

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Students are required to present a valid Food Safety Handler Certification.

description: This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry. Embark on a culinary adventure and taste the world! This engaging, hands-on course delves into the vibrant tapestry of global cuisines. Through the preparation of authentic and flavorful dishes, you'll explore the unique ingredients, techniques, and cultural significance that define cooking around the world. Emphasis will be placed on understanding and appreciating diverse flavor profiles, from the aromatic spices of Southeast Asia to the bold tastes of Latin America and the delicate herbs of the Mediterranean. Discover how regional ingredients and historical influences shape the distinctive character of each cuisine, and expand your culinary repertoire with a global perspective. Students are required to present a valid Food Safety Handler Certification and must wear the appropriate professional uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: Cooking for Special Diets

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Students are required to present a valid Food Handler Certificate. Basic cooking will not be taught; students should have foundational food preparation knowledge and skills prior to enrollment.

description: Essentials of planning and preparing meals for individuals with special dietary requirements. A variety of diets will be explored, including gluten-free, vegan, diabetic-friendly, low-sodium, allergen-free, and more. Students will gain knowledge and skills to prepare meals that cater to diverse dietary restrictions. Emphasis on nutritional requirements of each diet, ingredient substitutions, cooking techniques, and menu planning strategies. Basic cooking will not be taught; students should have foundational food preparation knowledge and skills prior to enrollment. Students are required to present a valid Food Handler Certificate.

title: Butchery & Charcuterie

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: HRM 52 and students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: This intensive course provides hands-on training in the creation and preparation of high-quality meat products and charcuterie. Students will learn to expertly examine, identify, and fabricate a variety of proteins, including poultry, beef, lamb, and pork. A strong emphasis will be placed on stringent safety and sanitation protocols throughout the program. Practical experience will be gained in crafting common charcuterie items, producing diverse sausages, applying various curing techniques, and mastering both hot and cold smoking methods. Students must possess a valid Food Safety Manager Certification and adhere to professional standards by wearing the required uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear, during all labs. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: Exploring Beverages
description: Study of grapes and winemaking, spirits processing, and beer making. History, geography, evaluation, and a comparative tasting of wines, spirits, and beers. Selection, storage, service of wines, wine lists, wine pricing. Evaluation of wine and food pairings. Exploration of nonalcoholic beverages and the role they play in the restaurant industry. Note: Students must be 21 years or older with valid photo identification (ID) in order to taste alcoholic beverages. Students under 21 years of age will not be allowed to consume alcoholic beverages.

title: Sustainability in Culinary Arts
description: Explore sustainability in culinary arts. Examine current thinking, trends, and production methods of food, before moving into the often hidden methods and difficulties in processing, storing, distributing, preparing, and consuming these foods. Various business models and management systems will be explored, with an emphasis on sustainable values that focus on profitability, environmental concerns, and consumer satisfaction. Farm-to-table ideals will be explored through the cultivation of organic vegetables.

title: Commercial Food Production

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: HRM 52 and CUL 102 and Students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of operations in a high-volume commercial kitchen, with an emphasis on food safety, production efficiency, and cost control. Students will engage in hands-on preparation of breakfast items, baked goods (yeast and quick breads, cookies, and desserts), and large-scale catering while learning batch cooking and production forecasting techniques. The course includes a retail sales component with Cafe 91 grab & go, modeled after operations such as Starbucks, where students rotate through front- and back-of-house roles, gaining experience in barista service, customer engagement, and point-of-sale systems. Additional topics include inventory management, financial oversight, sanitation protocols, and the full flow of food from ordering through service. Designed for students pursuing careers in culinary arts, hospitality, or institutional foodservice. Students are required to present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification and must wear the appropriate professional uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear.

title: Dining Room Service Management
description: Skills and knowledge needed for all aspects of dining room service. Exploration of the various styles of service. Table setting styles, buffet set-ups, wine and beverage service, and service as a sales tool are covered. The safety of both customer and staff are discussed.

title: Restaurant Operations

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: HRM 52 and CUL 103 . Students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.
Corequisite: CUL 114 (May have been taken previously)

description: This course provides hands-on experience in operating a student-run restaurant, with an emphasis on front-of-house and back-of-house coordination, customer service, and food safety. Students rotate through key service and kitchen stations, practicing essential skills such as point-of-sale (POS) operations, barista service, and standardized recipe execution. Through experiential learning in Cafe 91, students apply industry-standard procedures for service, food preparation, and equipment operation, preparing them for careers in restaurant and hospitality management. Students are required to present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification and must wear the appropriate professional uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: Artisan Bread
description: A systematic approach to bread, including details of mixing, fermenting, shaping, and baking bread. The course covers baker's math, ingredient selection and function, how mixing affects fermentation, and other bread baking fundamentals.

title: Specialty Cakes

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: CUL 106 . Students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: To participate in this course, students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification and wear the appropriate professional uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear. Unlock the secrets of exceptional cake creation! This course provides comprehensive instruction in diverse cake mixing methods, crafting delectable creams and fillings, and mastering professional assembly techniques. Through hands-on practice, you'll develop a strong foundation in cake design and decoration, moving from simple elegance to visually stunning complexity. By the end of the course, you'll be able to produce intricate cakes with sophisticated textures and unforgettable flavors. Students must possess a valid Food Safety Manager Certification and adhere to professional standards by wearing the required uniform, including non-slip kitchen footwear, during all labs. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: American Regional Cuisine

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: HRM 52 . Students must present a valid Food Safety Manager Certification.

description: This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry. American Regional Cooking is a flavorful journey through the diverse culinary landscape of the United States. From the hearty chowders of New England to the bold spices of the Southwest, this course explores iconic dishes and food traditions from every corner of the country - including the Mid-Atlantic, Deep South, West Coast, and beyond. Discover how geography, culture, and history have shaped America's regional cuisines, and gain hands-on experience preparing a variety of classic and contemporary recipes that celebrate the nation's rich food heritage. This course is intended for students interested in pursuing a career in Culinary Arts or Baking and Pastry.

title: Food Service Entrepreneurship
description: This project-based course introduces students to the entrepreneurial process in food service. Students will explore and examine the process of planning, developing, financing, and managing the operational aspects of launching a new foodservice operation, including restaurants, food trucks, home cottage, microenterprise home kitchen operation, and emerging alternatives. Drawing on core hospitality management concepts, the course guides students through the creation and evaluation of a comprehensive business plan for a foodservice operation concept. Emphasis is placed on critical decision-making, innovation, market research, feasibility analysis, and financial forecasting. The course will use a variety of media, such as case studies, real-life experiences, and interviews.

title: Ballet Fundamentals
description: Fundamental terminology, technique, and movement combinations for ballet. Includes ballet floor work, ballet barre, center practice, floor progressions, and musicality and phrasing.

title: Ballet I
description: Beginning terminology, technique, and movement combinations for ballet. Includes barre work, center floor work, floor progressions, preparation for turning, and musicality and phrasing.

title: Ballet II
description: Intermediate technique, vocabulary, and movement combinations for ballet. Includes intermediate barre work, demi-pointe work, use of epaulement and increasingly difficult center floor combinations.

title: Ballet Performance
description: Advanced barre work, center work, floor progressions, and performance of classical ballet variations for ballet dance.

title: Choreography

requirements.raw: Advisory: DNCE 12A or DNCE 12B or DNCE 13

description: Techniques of choreography and dance composition. Designed for the experienced dancer.

title: Latin Dance I
description: Latin styles of dance. Includes Cha Cha, Samba, Rumba, Pasodoble and Jive.

title: Modern Fundamentals
description: Fundamental vocabulary, technique, and movement combinations for Modern Dance. Includes floor work, center work, floor progressions, musicality and phrasing.

title: Social Dance Forms I
description: Fundamentals of music, dance positions, dance formations, and choreography to be used in the study of, but not limited to Swing, Salsa, Waltz, Foxtrot, and Tango.

title: Social Dance Forms II
description: Advanced study of dance positions, dance formations, music, and choreography to be used in the study of, but not limited to, Swing, Salsa, Waltz, Foxtrot, and Tango.

title: Modern I
description: Beginning terminology, technique, and movement combinations for Modern dance.

title: Modern II
description: Intermediate terminology, technique, and movement combinations for Modern dance. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Modern Performance
description: Performance aspects of Modern dance, including advanced terminology, technique, choreographic elements, and performance for the experienced dance student.

title: Jazz I
description: Beginning vocabulary, technique, and movement combinations for jazz dance. Includes warm-up, progressions, and center floor routines.

title: Jazz II
description: Intermediate vocabulary, technique, and movement combinations for jazz dance. Includes warm-up, progressions, and center floor routines.

title: Jazz Performance
description: Introduces the experienced dancer to the performance styles and techniques of jazz dance. Includes advanced warm-up, floor progressions, and performance of complex jazz dance routines.

title: Jazz Fundamentals
description: Introduces fundamental vocabulary, technique, and movement combinations for jazz dance. Includes floor work, center work, floor progressions, routines, and musicality and phrasing.

title: Tap I
description: Beginning level technique, rhythms, and routines for tap dance.

title: Tap II
description: Intermediate technique, rhythms, and routines for tap dance.

title: Tap Performance
description: Introduces the experienced dancer to the performance aspects of tap by providing advanced techniques leading to the performance of compositions.

title: Dance Rehearsal
description: Beginning rehearsal elements for the experienced dancer participating in concert production, competitions and community performances. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Dance Production
description: Intermediate choreography to perform on stage and at competitions. Students will apply choreographic skill, conduct stage rehearsals, and learn costuming techniques. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Dance Ensemble
description: Small ensemble dance experience with a focus on production elements. Includes experience in story development, choreography, and performance culminating in the practical application of a series of public presentations. Attendance is required at all public performances including off-campus locations.

title: Theater Dance I
description: Beginning theatre dance variations drawn from a variety of theater musicals and movies. Includes concepts of acting and staging incorporated with musical theater choreography.

title: Theater Dance II
description: Advanced theatre dance variations for the technically skilled dancer drawn from a variety of theater musicals and movies. Includes concepts of acting and staging incorporated with musical theater choreography.

title: Contemporary Dance
description: Intermediate to advanced terminology, technique, and movement combinations for Contemporary dance.

title: Classical Dance
description: Advanced ballet repertoire focusing on the different schools of technique including Balanchine, Bournonville, and Vaganova.

title: Commercial Dance
description: Beginning terminology, styles, techniques, and movement combinations for Hip Hop dance. Includes Hip Hop choreographic skills.

title: Improvisation
description: Beginning to advanced improvisation in dance and choreography.

title: Dance Directives
description: Provides the intermediate or advanced student the practical experience to assist an instructor in the creation and instruction of a dance class.

title: Repertory
description: Advanced choreography and repertory to perform at workshops, competitions, and special events. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Commercial Dance II
description: Intermediate to advanced terminology, styles, and movement combinations for Hip Hop dance. Includes Hip Hop choreographic skills.

title: Pilates Fundamentals
description: Pilates foundation mat-work. Conditioning exercises and body awareness resulting in improved alignment, strength, flexibility, control, and coordination. Includes an introduction to the Pilates Reformer.

title: Conditioning Through Dance
description: Improves fitness through the coordination of dance exercises. Focuses on strength, flexibility, and range of motion. Designed for the dancer and non-dancer.

title: Pilates I
description: Pilates beginning and intermediate mat-work and beginning Reformer. Includes Pilatesstick and the Magic Circle.

title: Pilates II
description: Pilates intermediate mat, reformer, and Pilatesstick and beginning Wunda Chair, step barrel, and Ped-a-Pul. Includes use of physioball in mat work.

title: Pilates III
description: Pilates intermediate and advanced mat, reformer (with use of Jumpboard), Wunda Chair (with use of split pedal), and Pilatesstick. Includes beginning Cadillac and High Barrel.

title: Dance Audition Techniques
description: Dance audition preparation, practice, and skill development for the commercial industry. Designed for the intermediate or advanced dancer.

title: Introduction to Dance
description: A survey of the profession of dance through lecture, discussion, demonstration, and participation. Includes philosophies, historical overviews of each genre, and the study of vocational roles in dance. This course will include participation and a general overview in dance forms such as ballet, modern, jazz, and cultural dance.

title: History and Appreciation of Dance
description: Theatrical dance in western civilization. History of dance in chronological sequence emphasizing the cultural background and historical development of various forms and styles of dance to include discussion of the influence of theatrical dance on other art forms.

title: Theory and Principles of Pilates

requirements.raw: Corequisite: DNCE 39 (may have been taken previously)

description: Teaching skills for the Pilates method of physical and mental conditioning. Concepts and principles as applied to the mat and apparatus repertoire.

title: Functional Anatomy for Pilates
description: Functional human anatomy as applied to the Pilates method of conditioning.

title: Teaching Pilates Mat Repertoire

requirements.raw: Corequisite: DN-T 27 (may have been taken previously)

description: Learning to teach the Pilates mat exercises and principles. Includes basic, intermediate, and advanced levels focusing on pedagogy and the development of correct neuromuscular patterning.

title: Teaching Pilates Reformer Repertoire
description: Learning to teach the Pilates Reformer exercises and principles. All levels are covered with a focus on the development of correct neuromuscular patterning.

title: Pilates Teaching-Mat and Reformer
description: Prepares students to teach Pilates in a variety of settings and situations. Teaching reinforces knowledge and understanding of the Pilates exercises. Includes lecture, observation, self-integration, assistant teaching, one-on-one teaching, and content. Off-campus observations may be required.

title: Teaching Pilates Cadillac and Wunda Chair Repertoire

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: DN-T 27 and DN-T 29 and DN-T 30

description: Learning to teach the Pilates repertoire of exercises on the Cadillac and Wunda Chair. All levels are covered with a focus on the development of correct neuromuscular patterning.

title: Teaching Pilates Ped-a-Pul, Barrels and Auxiliary Equipment Repertoire
description: Learning to teach Pilates exercises on the following apparatus: Ped-a-Pul, Ladder Barrel, Step Barrel, Arc Barrel, Magic Circle, C-cushion, and props. All levels are covered with a focus on the development of correct neuromuscular patterning.

title: Pilates Teaching-Cadillac, Wunda Chair, & Auxiliary Equipment
description: Prepares students to teach Pilates in a variety of settings and situations. Teaching reinforces knowledge and understanding of the Pilates exercises and concepts. Includes lecture, observation, self-integration, assistant teaching, and one-on-one teaching. Off-campus observations may be required.

title: Dance Teaching Methods

requirements.raw: Corequisite: DNCE 2B (may have been taken previously) and DNCE 12B (may have been taken previously) and DNCE 14B (may have been taken previously)

description: The application of pedagogical methods in dance. Explores teaching strategies, imagery, motivational techniques, music for class instruction, and injury prevention. Focus is on the genres of ballet, jazz, and modern dance. Course will involve on- and off-campus dance teaching observations.

title: Principles of Microeconomics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Placement as determined by the college's multiple measures assessment process or completion of a course taught at or above the level of elementary algebra.

description: An introductory course using microeconomic models to understand individual decisions by consumers and firms, market outcomes including market failure, elasticity, market structures, labor markets, inequality, and the impact of government policies.

title: Principles of Microeconomics - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Placement as determined by the college's multiple measures assessment process or completion of a course taught at or above the level of elementary algebra and acceptance into the Honors Program

description: An introductory course using microeconomic models to understand individual decisions by consumers and firms, market outcomes including market failure, elasticity, market structures, labor markets, inequality, and the impact of government policies. This is an honors course. May not earn credit for both ECON C2001H and ECON C2001 .

title: Principles of Macroeconomics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Placement as determined by the college's multiple measures assessment process or completion of a course taught at or above the level of elementary algebra.

description: An introductory course using models of the domestic and international economy to understand national income, unemployment, inflation, economic growth, inequality, the financial system, and monetary, fiscal, and other economic policies.

title: Principles of Macroeconomics - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Placement as determined by the college's multiple measures assessment process or completion of a course taught at or above the level of elementary algebra and acceptance into the Honors Program.

description: An introductory course using models of the domestic and international economy to understand national income, unemployment, inflation, economic growth, inequality, the financial system, and monetary, fiscal, and other economic policies. This is an honors course. May not earn credit for both ECON C2002H and ECON C2002 .

title: Applied Business Statistics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MATH 71 or eligibility for ( STAT C1000 or MATH 110) or (STAT C1000H or MATH 110H)

description: Statistical reasoning and application of primary statistical techniques used in solving managerial problems. Topics include collection and interpretation of data, measures of central tendency and dispersion, probability distributions, sampling and estimation, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, linear regression, and correlation and index numbers.

title: Introduction to Education

requirements.raw: Advisory: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Concepts and issues related to teaching diverse learners in contemporary public schools (K-12). Topics include historical and philosophical foundations of the American education system, teaching as a profession and career, contemporary education issues, California Content Standards and framework, and teacher performance standards. In addition to class time, 45-hours of structured fieldwork are required at an approved public school elementary classrooms with a certified classroom teacher and students that represent California's diverse population. Proof of a negative TB test and fingerprint clearance are required for classroom observations.

title: Aspects and Issues in Teaching

requirements.raw: Advisory: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Survey of the K-12 teaching profession, including teaching and learning styles, common core standards and testing, current California and national legislation, social issues, school funding, and teacher and student rights and responsibilities. Off-campus assignments required. TB test and observations required.

title: Introduction to Mechatronics
description: A combination of conventional electronic technology with mechanical and computer technology. Special emphasis is on robotics. Hands-on activities include the building of a robot.

title: Technical Applications in Microcomputers
description: Personal computer (PC) applications used in electronics technology. Includes word processing, spreadsheets, computer presentation methods, and internet research specifically designed for electronics technology.

title: Computer Simulation and Troubleshooting
description: Troubleshooting of electronic hardware, including use of computer-based tools for simulation and troubleshooting of analog and digital circuits. National Instruments Multisim software will be used for circuit analysis, value substitution, and fault diagnostics.

title: Electronic Circuits - Direct Current (DC)
description: Direct Current (DC) electrical circuits and their applications. Covers DC sources, analysis, test equipment, measurements, and troubleshooting of resistive devices and other basic components. Includes Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff's law, and network theorems. (Students seeking a survey course in electronics should take ELEC 10 , Introduction to Mechatronics, rather than ELEC 50A or 50B .)

title: Electronic Circuits (AC)
description: Alternating Current (AC) electrical circuits and their applications. Covers AC sources, analysis (using complex numbers), test equipment, measurements, and troubleshooting of basic circuits with capacitors, inductors, and resistors. Includes impedance, resonance, filters, and decibels.

title: Semiconductor Devices and Circuits
description: Solid-state devices and circuits, including bipolar-junction and field-effect transistors, rectifier diodes, operational amplifiers, and thyristors. Analog circuits studied include discrete and integrated circuit amplifiers, voltage regulators, oscillators and timers. Emphasizes configurations, classes, load lines, characteristic curves, gain, troubleshooting, measurements, and frequency response.

title: Communications Systems
description: Analog and digital communications systems. Emphasizes analog and digital modulation principles, multiplexing, protocols, and telecommunications circuits and systems.

title: Industrial Electronics
description: Industrial electronic components and basic control circuits. Includes time delay controls, thyristor controls, relays, optoelectronic (opto) devices, direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) motor control, transducers, silicon controlled rectifier (SCR) and unijunction transistor (UJT) devices.

title: Industrial Electronic Systems
description: Systems application of industrial electronics including industrial production and processes, automation, and programmable and motor controllers. Emphasis is on programmable logic controllers (PLCs).

title: Microwave Communications
description: Microwave components and circuits. Stresses transmission lines, Smith Charts, impedance matching, antenna characteristics, wave propagation, frequency analysis, and measurement techniques.

title: Digital Electronics
description: Combinational and sequential logic circuits emphasizing number systems, binary math, basic gates, Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps, encoders, decoders, multiplexing, flip-flops, counters, registers, and microcontrollers. Stresses design and troubleshooting techniques. Includes finite state machine design, Algorithmic State Machine (ASM) charts, field programmable logic arrays (FPGAs) and associated software.

title: Electronic Assembly and Fabrication
description: Manufacturing and fabrication processes associated with the electronics industry. Printed circuit board (PCB) design from conception to completion. Emphasizes electrical schematics, bill of material (BOM), component selection, layout design, manufacturability, assembly, soldering, de-soldering, and surface-mount technology.

title: Advanced Surface Mount Assembly and Rework
description: Advanced course in assembly and repair (soldering) on surface mount assemblies (SMT). Material is similar in content to the Institute for Printed Circuits (IPC) surface mount assembly and rework certification.

title: Microcontroller Systems
description: Microcontroller systems and programming methods; programmable logic devices (PLDs); serial communications; conversion of signals from analog to digital formats and the converse. Industry applications, interfacing, and troubleshooting.

title: FCC General Radiotelephone Operator License Preparation
description: Prepares qualified electronics and aviation technicians for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) commercial General Radiotelephone Operator License (GROL).

title: Laboratory Studies in Electronics Technology
description: Extended laboratory experience supplementary to that available in the regular program. Allows the student to pursue more advanced and complex laboratory projects and experiments.

title: Work Experience in Electronics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course.

description: Provides on-the-job experience in electronics at an approved work site which is related to classroom instruction. A minimum of five hours per week of supervised work (54 clock hours per semester) is required for each one unit of credit.

title: Paramedic Preparatory Course

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Eligibility for READ 90 and Completed Paramedic Program application AND current California EMT certificate and 1000 hours employment as an EMT.

description: Assessment and review of required Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) competencies as part of the preparation for the Paramedic Academy. Includes current practices, medical terminology, mathematical skills for drug calculations, and applied physiology and anatomy of human body systems.

title: Paramedic Core Content
description: Didactic and psychomotor paramedic core content including anatomy, pathophysiology, and pharmacology for paramedics.

title: Emergency Care for Paramedics
description: Familiarizes the paramedic with the normal, abnormal, and diseased heart, patient assessments, assessment tools, interpretation of dysrhythmias, and paramedic interventions. Certifies students in Pediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS), and Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) in accordance with the American Heart Association (AHA).

title: Paramedic Skills Competency
description: Paramedic skills required for field operation as a paramedic and for licensing in competency-based exams.

title: Paramedic Clinical Internship

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: EMS 10 and EMS 40 and EMS 50

description: Clinical experience and application of paramedic theory and practice with an emphasis on patient assessment and utilization of paramedic skills in a hospital setting.

title: Paramedic Field Externship

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: EMS 70 and successful completion of Los Angeles County accreditation exam.

description: Application of concepts of paramedic theory and practices, with emphasis on patient assessment and utilization of paramedic skills in a field setting on an operational paramedic unit.

title: CADD and Digital Design Media Level I
description: Computer Aided Design and Drafting (CADD) Level 1 and computer applications in building construction, engineering, and related fields, including spreadsheet and presentation applications. Field trips required.

title: Legal Aspects of Construction

requirements.raw: Advisory: ECT 70 taken prior or concurrently

description: Legal aspects of the construction industry involving the owner, contractor, builder or developer, and design professional. Includes codes, licensing, contracts, bonds, and lien laws. May include off-campus assignments.

title: Civil Engineering Technology and CADD
description: Theory of civil engineering projects with hands-on instruction in civil drawings and Computer Aided Drafting and Design (CADD) applications. Layout, topography maps, grading plans, sections, street improvements, and interpretation of surveyor's data are covered. Set of CADD drawings produced for a final portfolio.

title: Reading Construction Drawings
description: Reading construction drawings as they apply to architecture, construction, interior design, and related fields. Off-campus assignments may be required.

title: Elements of Construction Management
description: Construction processes, terminology, and procedures. Topics include construction careers, building systems, sustainability, quality control, management, and scheduling of resources (materials, equipment, time, personnel, and finance).

title: Construction Estimating
description: Construction estimating and bidding procedures using contract documents, construction drawings, and cost data. Estimating methods and use of estimating forms or software, including detailed quantity take-offs of building materials and labor required in building construction.

title: Fundamentals of Construction Inspection
description: Construction inspection of light frame wood construction and steel structures. Topics include vertical and horizontal loads, stress analysis, framing and structural standards of lumber and steel, metallurgy, and welding.

title: Engineering Design Technology Work Experience

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course.

description: Provides on-the-job experience at an approved worksite which is related to classroom instruction in Engineering Design Technology. A minimum of 54 paid or unpaid clock hours per semester of supervised work is required for each unit of credit. If this is a volunteer program on or off campus, a minimum number of hours per month will be required as part of the 54 hour total.

title: Introduction to Engineering
description: Engineering professions including academic requirements, licensure, articulation agreements with four-year institutions, transfer, engineering study as a preparation for other careers, and academic and employment strategies. Engineering design, creativity, and problem-solving processes including working as a team member on an engineering design project. Field trips are required.

title: Engineering Critical Thinking

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: A critical thinking course for science and engineering students. Analyze, criticize, and reason inductively and deductively and reach well-supported factual or judgmental conclusions. Main topics include: identifying topics for investigation, developing planning strategies, locating pertinent information, critically analyzing sources of information, testing hypotheses, synthesizing and organizing results for effective written and verbal communication. Students will complete a hands-on experience with a client-centered engineering design project to develop critical thinking skills.

title: Engineering Design, Environment and Society
description: Engineering Design, Society and Environment is an integrated lecture-lab, project-based and problem-based semester-long course with an external community-based partnership. In this course we explore the role of the engineer and engineering design within our society, the use of natural resources, and the built environment. We also incorporate technical drawings, CAD modelling, mechanical systems, machine tools, fabrication, applied physics, sustainability, environmental justice, social inequity, research and design methodology, teamwork, communication, and engineering ethics. We evaluate our learning through documentation of laboratory activities, development of authentic project solutions with industry standard tools, and critical self-reflection.

title: Introduction to Engineering Programming Concepts and Methodologies
description: Fundamental concepts of procedure-oriented programming, associated abstraction mechanisms and design processes, interface of software with the physical world, use of sensors, and application of numerical techniques.

title: Programming Applications for Engineers
description: Engineering computation using MATLAB and Simulink. Topics include matrix computation, statistical analysis, graphics, and numerical methods. Common examples and applications of physics and engineering are used throughout the course.

title: Properties of Materials

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: CHEM 50 or CHEM 50H or CHEM 55 and PHYS 2AG or PHYS 4A

description: Mechanical, electrical, magnetic, optical, and thermal properties of engineering materials and their relation to the materials' internal structure. Atomic structure and bonding, crystalline structures, phase and phase diagrams, metals, polymers, ceramics, composites, mechanical deformation and fracture, structural control and influence of properties, materials naming and designating systems, corrosion process, lasers, semiconductors, and electronic packaging materials.

title: Introduction to Digital Electronics with FPGA Programming
description: A core course in electrical and computer engineering which introduces Digital Electronics and Field Programmable Gate Array programming. Digital circuit implementation using Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). Analysis, design, building, and testing of combinational and sequential digital logic circuits. Analysis and design of finite state machines with state diagrams and ASM charts. Design of finite state machines with HDL and implementation of finite state machines with FPGAs.

title: Introduction to Engineering Graphics
description: Engineering graphics and problem solving techniques using orthographic, auxiliary, isometric, and oblique view drawings. Skills in freehand and instrument drawing are developed and applied to the solution of engineering problems.

title: Engineering Graphics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MATH 150 or (eligibility for MATH 160 or eligibility for MATH 180 ) and ( ENGR 18 or instructor approval)

description: Project-based learning activities and hands-on design related to 2D and 3D Computer-Aided Design (CAD) for engineering students. The principles of engineering drawing and sketching for civil and mechanical design, the use of computer graphics and solid modeling in design representation of 3D objects, assembly, and simulation as well as American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) standards on geometric dimensioning and tolerances.

title: Statics
description: Vector approach to static equilibrium of rigid bodies, forces, and couples in two- and three-dimensional space. Application of equilibrium principles to trusses, frames, and machines. Calculation of center of mass and centroid. Friction, moment of inertia, and distributed and concentrated loads. Forces in cables and beams. Fluid statics. Introduction to virtual work.

title: Applied Statics
description: Vector approach to static equilibrium of rigid bodies, forces, and couples in two- and three-dimensional space. Application of equilibrium principles to trusses, frames, and machines. Calculation of center of mass and centroid. Friction, moment of inertia, and distributed and concentrated loads. Forces in cables and beams. Fluid statics. Introduction to virtual work. This course is for applied Engineering students. This course may not be accepted in general engineering transfer programs.

title: Dynamics
description: Vector approach to classical mechanics including absolute and relative motion of particles and rigid bodies in translational and rotational motion. Instantaneous center of rotation. Application of Newton's Second Law, work-energy and impulse-momentum methods, and introduction to mechanical vibrations.

title: Mechanics of Materials
description: Mechanics of deformable bodies subjected to axial, torsional, shearing, and bending loads. Includes combined stresses, statically indeterminate structures, deflection and stress analysis of beams, stability of columns, strain energy methods, and design of pressure vessels and structures. Applied concepts through a laboratory experience linking mechanics of materials to properties of materials.

title: Electrical Engineering

requirements.raw: Corequisite: ENGR 285 (may have been taken previously) or MATH 290 (may have been taken previously)

description: Electrical circuit analysis including applications of Kirchoff's Laws and Thevenin's Theorems to direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC) circuits. Fundamental principles, including steady state and transient circuit response, complex impedance and admittance, Fourier and Laplace transforms, and three-phase circuits. Application of fundamental circuit principles to operational amplifier and transistor circuits.

title: Robotics Team Project Development

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required for robotics competition team members.

description: This course is for members of the Robotics Team. Introduces the knowledge, skills and activities needed to organize, promote and manage the design phase of a robotics competition team. Includes a survey of problem analysis, programming, mechanical design, and project management. Intended for students with an interest in robotics who need to gain experience as members of an engineering design team. Instructor approval required.

title: Intermediate Robotics Team Project Development

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required for robotics competition team members.

description: For members of the robotics team who compete in one or more intercollegiate competitions. Designing a solution to a complex problem by applying strategic design, mechanical design, computer-aided design, numerical modeling, computer programming, prototyping, fabrication, and project management. Instructor approval required. Off-campus activities required.

title: Special Projects in Engineering
description: Offers selected students recognition for their academic interests and ability and the opportunity to explore their disciplines in greater depth. The content of each course and the methods of study vary from semester to semester and depend on the particular project under consideration. Student must have instructor's authorization before enrolling in this class. Prior instructor approval and approved independent learning contract required. Field trips may be required.

title: Differential Equations and Linear Algebra for Engineers
description: Linear algebra, ordinary and partial differential equations, systems of differential equations, Fourier series, and Laplace and Fourier transforms and their applications in engineering. Applications include mechanics, vibration, circuits, and computer vision.

title: Foundations of Technical Sales

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MATH 150 or eligibility for MATH 160

description: Technical sales course for science and engineering students. Fundamentals of technical sales including communication, business knowledge basics, leadership, sales and ethics. Main topics include understanding technical sales as a member of the sales process, technical marketing and prequalification, successful customer engagements, decision makers and technical buyers, the trusted advisor, the perfect pitch and demo, RFPs and financial justification.

title: Technical Sales Strategies
description: Case studies and experiential lessons on the development and application of technical sales strategies. Specific topics will include developing pricing and distribution strategies, managing a sales staff and channel, developing sales teams and global sales plans, bid and negotiation strategies, time management skills, and implementing sales automation technologies.

title: Academic Reading and Writing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Placement as determined by the college's multiple measures assessment process.

description: In this course, students receive instruction in academic reading and writing, including writing processes, effective use of language, analytical thinking, and the foundations of academic research.

title: Academic Reading and Writing - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Placement as determined by the college's multiple measures assessment process and Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: In this course, students receive instruction in academic reading and writing, including writing processes, effective use of language, analytical thinking, and the foundations of academic research. This is an honors course. No credit for both ENGL C1000 and ENGL C1000H.

title: Critical Thinking and Writing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: In this course, students receive instruction in critical thinking for purposes of constructing, evaluating, and composing arguments in a variety of rhetorical forms, using primarily non-fiction texts, refining writing skills and research strategies developed in ENGL C1000 College Reading and Writing (or C-ID ENGL 100) or similar first-year college writing course.

title: Critical Thinking and Writing - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A and acceptance into the Honors Program

description: In this course, students receive instruction in critical thinking for purposes of constructing, evaluating, and composing arguments in a variety of rhetorical forms, using primarily non-fiction texts, refining writing skills and research strategies developed in ENGL C1000 College Reading and Writing (or C-ID ENGL 100) or similar first-year college writing course. This is an honors course.

title: Introduction to Literature

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: In this course, students are introduced to works by diverse authors and major literary genres, developing close reading and analytical writing skills. Students also develop appreciation for and critical understanding of the cultural, historical, and aesthetic qualities of literature.

title: Introduction to Literature - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: In this course, students are introduced to works by diverse authors and major literary genres, developing close reading and analytical writing skills. Students also develop appreciation for and critical understanding of the cultural, historical, and aesthetic qualities of literature. This is an honors course. May not earn credit for both ENGL C1002H and ENGL C1002 .

title: Creative Writing - Fiction

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Eligibility for ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A .

description: Elements, processes, and techniques of fiction writing. Includes genre, setting, point of view, character development, plot development, description, and dialogue with an emphasis on student development as a writer of fiction through practice and discussion.

title: Creative Writing - Poetry

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Eligibility for ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Emphasizes the student's development as a poet.

title: Creative Writing - Memoir

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Analysis and writing of memoirs including stylistic and syntactic forms and composition strategies used when writing memoir.

title: Creative Writing - Nonfiction

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Analysis and writing of creative nonfiction including stylistic and syntactic forms and composition strategies used when writing creative nonfiction.

title: Grammar Review
description: Fundamentals of English for the student who needs a practical course focusing on usage and grammar: subjects, verbs, agreement, case, fragments, modifiers, parallelism, shifts in construction, and punctuation.

title: Paragraph Writing
description: Analysis and writing of paragraphs. Through the process of writing, the student learns to state and support an idea about a focused topic.

title: Writing Fundamentals

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Satisfactory score on the English Placement Test or completion of LERN 81
