Multiple integrals in various coordinate systems with applications. Vector fields, line integrals, and independence of path. Green's Theorem, surface integrals, flux, divergence, and curl. Stokes' Theorem and the Divergence Theorem.

title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
description: First order ordinary differential equations, with applications and numerical methods. Solutions to higher order differential equations using undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, and power series, with applications. Solutions to linear and non-linear systems of differential equations, including numerical solutions. Matrix algebra, solutions of linear systems of equations, and determinants. Vector spaces, linear independence, basis and dimension, subspace and inner product space, including the Gram-Schmidt procedure. Linear transformations, kernel and range, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization and symmetric matrices.

title: Differential Equations
description: First-order ordinary differential equations, including separable, linear, homogeneous, Bernoulli, and exact, with applications and numerical methods. Solutions to higher-order differential equations using undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, power series, and Laplace transforms, with applications. Solutions to linear and non-linear systems of differential equations, including numerical solutions.

title: Medical Terminology
description: This course is an introduction to the use and meaning of the medical terminology used in various allied health fields.

title: Introduction to Interviewing and Counseling
description: Theory and practice in interviewing skills. Stresses application of counseling theories, helping skills, and consultation theories to allow exploration of self as a helper and learn facilitating skills to bring about change. Emphasis on establishing rapport, obtaining information, and developing a supportive relationship in a variety of mental health settings.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing for Psychiatric Technicians

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Admission to the Psychiatric Technician Program

description: Holistic approach to assessment and intervention in the care of the medical-surgical patient. Examines physiological modes of rest and exercise, regulation, circulation, ventilation, reproductive, elimination, and the sensory system; medical-surgical nursing; care of the dying patient and cardiovascular problems; calculations of drug dosage and administration of medications; study of anatomy and physiology of the human body.

title: Medical-Surgical Clinical Experience
description: Application, assessment, intervention, and evaluation of nursing treatment in the physiological modes of rest and exercise, regulation, nutrition, elimination, application of emergency procedures, circulation, ventilation, fluids, and electrolytes. Psychosocial aspects of care including interdependence, role function, self-concept, care of aged, and cultural aspects. Development and application of nursing skills for those with medical-surgical problems and special needs. Calculation and administration of medications. Roy's Adaptation Model serves as the conceptual framework.

title: Advanced Medical-Surgical Nursing and Pharmacology for Psychiatric Technician (PT)
description: Concepts of nursing assessment and intervention for disease processes affecting body systems. Principles related to the safe administration of medications including classifications of medications and knowledge of specific medications. Roy's Adaptation Model serves as the conceptual framework.

title: Advanced Medical-Surgical Nursing for Psychiatric Technicians Clinical
description: The application of nursing skills to patients with medical-surgical disorders which includes administration of medications utilizing the Nursing Process. Sister Callista Roy's Adaptation Model serves as the conceptual framework.

title: Introduction to Psychiatric Technology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Admission to Mental Health Technology - Psychiatric Technician Program

description: Role and function of the Psychiatric Technician. Includes mental health theories of personality development, self-concept, role function, and interdependence. Also includes developmental disabilities theories of sensorimotor techniques and positive behavior support techniques.

title: Introduction to Psychiatric Technology Clinical
description: Clinical experience at mental health facilities within the community which serve individuals diagnosed with mental health and/or intellectual, physical, and other developmental disabilities. Acceptance into the Psychiatric Technician Program is required to take this course.

title: Nursing Care of the Developmentally Disabled Person

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MENT 56 and MENT 56L and MENT 70 and MENT 70L

description: Knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to safely teach individuals diagnosed with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Techniques of positive behavior intervention and support, behavior modification, and sensorimotor training are used, focusing on maximizing independence. Examines typical and atypical development and lifespan issues from infancy to end of life. Examines etiologies related to developmental disabilities.

title: Nursing Care of the Developmentally Disabled Person - Clinical
description: Application of skills needed to teach and provide care for individuals diagnosed with developmental disabilities.

title: Psychiatric Nursing for Psychiatric Technicians Clinical

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MENT 56 and MENT 56L and Admission to Psychiatric Technician Program.

description: Clinical instruction in the assessment and treatment of individuals diagnosed with mental disorders.

title: Psychiatric Nursing for Psychiatric Technicians

requirements.raw: Corequisite: MENT 73L and ( PSYC C1000 or PSYC 1A) or (PSYC C1000H or PSYC 1AH) (may have been taken previously)

description: Theoretical instruction in the assessment and treatment of individuals diagnosed with mental disorders. Includes medications used in the treatment of mental disorders, therapeutic communication and other therapeutic techniques, and assertiveness and leadership skills necessary for safe practice as a licensed Psychiatric Technician.

title: Work Experience in Mental Health Technology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MENT 72 and MENT 73T and Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.

description: Provides students with on-the-job experience in the field of mental health, nursing skills, addiction paraprofessional training, and/or developmental disability, related to classroom instruction, at an approved work site. On-the-job experience at an approved work site. Requires 108 hours for 2 units.

title: Weather and the Atmospheric Environment
description: Processes that influence weather and climate: seasonality, structure of the atmosphere, atmospheric stability, severe weather (hurricanes, tornadoes, thunderstorms), climate change, and the causes and effects of air pollution. Students will use a variety of weather instruments and the course may include either field-work or field trips.

title: Weather and Atmospheric Environment Laboratory

requirements.raw: Corequisite: METO 3 (May have been taken previously)

description: Laboratory applications and problem solving related to the atmospheric environment. Emphasizes the collection and analysis of weather and climate data.

title: Medical Microbiology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( CHEM 10 or CHEM 40 ) and ( BIOL 1 or BIOL 4 or BIOL 4H )

description: Fundamental concepts of medical microbiology including a survey of microbial classification, morphology, physiology, and genetics; beneficial and pathological aspects; growth and control of microbes; bacteriology, virology, mycology, and parasitology, immunology, epidemiology, and host-microbe interactions. In addition to the biological characteristics of microbes, principles of disease transmission, prevention, pathogenesis, antimicrobial resistance, laboratory diagnosis of infectious diseases, opportunists and the human microbiome will be explored. Laboratory exercises examine microbial morphology, physiology, and genetics as well as environmental influences of microorganisms. Laboratory techniques include culturing, examining, and identifying microorganisms. Field trips are required.

title: Microbiology

requirements.raw: Advisory: BIOL 1 or BIOL 4 or BIOL 4H

description: Fundamental concepts of microbiology including viruses, bacteria, fungi, protozoa and parasitic worms.

title: Introduction to Immunology

requirements.raw: Advisory: BIOL 1 or BIOL 4 or BIOL 4H

description: Immunology including principles of innate and adaptive immunity, B and T lymphocyte structure, function, and development, the major histocompatibility complex, immune system errors, and applications and techniques in the immunology field as they pertain to medical diagnostics, immunohistochemistry, and biotechnology.

title: Fundamentals of Audio Technology
description: Fundamental terminology, equipment, techniques, and technical concepts related to audio technology. Topics include the basic principles and practices of signal flow, analog audio, digital audio, computer workstations, musical instrument digital interface (MIDI), synthesis, and sound recording utilizing modern hardware and software. These topics will be explored from a technical perspective.

title: Acoustics for Audio Production
description: Scientific and practical concepts of acoustic sound for audio production. Topics include the science of sound, sound generation, sound in the free field, acoustic spaces, psychoacoustics, and techniques for acoustic management. Students will be able to critically analyze acoustic phenomena and apply this knowledge in audio production settings.

title: Introduction to Music Production
description: Creative techniques and elements of electronic audio. Topics include digital audio workstations, musical instrument digital interface (MIDI), synthesis, sampling, sequencing, editing, composition, arranging, and mixing. Compositions are expected of students utilizing electronic audio techniques.

title: Business of Audio Production
description: Business and legal aspects of the audio industry. Topics include contracts, publishing, licensing, distribution, and copyright. In addition, the duties and responsibilities of producers, agents, managers, promoters, and performing artists will be examined. Students will gain a firm understanding of past and current business practices related to audio production.

title: Audio Recording
description: Intermediate concepts and skills for audio recording. Topics include recording techniques, signal flow, microphone principles and usage, equipment, signal processing, digital audio workstation recording functions, and recording procedures. Students will produce quality audio recordings from a variety of sound sources.

title: Live Sound Engineering
description: Intermediate concepts and skills for audio engineering live events. Topics will include microphones, mixers, amplifiers, monitoring, setup and teardown, sound reinforcement, cabling and wiring, and duties and roles for stages, clubs, theaters, churches, and industrial venues. Students will be able to engineer a multi-input live sound performance.

title: Audio Production
description: Advanced studio-recording techniques. Topics include recording sessions, applied acoustics, multi-microphone configurations, overdub sessions, cue mixes, control room configuration, roles and duties, editing, and mixing. Students will learn to apply audio technology and recording concepts in a multitrack studio environment.

title: Audio for Multimedia
description: Intermediate creative, technical, and collaborative techniques for producing audio for recorded multimedia. Topics include games, animation, video, commercials, radio, virtual reality, Internet, and motion graphics. Students will be able to produce quality audio tracks for use in a variety of multimedia settings.

title: Sound Performance and Synthesis
description: Advanced creative, technical, and collaborative skills for synthesizing, designing, and performing sound. Topics will cover synthesis and sound design for a variety of purposes, such as music performances, film, TV, multimedia, games, animations, concerts, theater performances, dance performances, theme parks, and artistic and commercial installations. Students will create and perform productions that they have designed and synthesized from scratch.

title: Songwriting
description: Processes and techniques of songwriting. Songs will be analyzed on chord structure, form, rhythm, melody, harmony, and lyrics. Original compositions and performances are expected from all students.

title: Audio Capstone

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MUSA 120 and MUSA 130 and MUSA 150 and MUSA 160

description: Advanced creative, organizational, and leadership skills for large-scale audio productions. Students will lead complex multi-track, multi-artist productions from conceptualization to delivery.

title: Work Experience in Audio Arts

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MUSA 150 or MUSA 160 or MUSA 210 and Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog

description: Job experience in audio production in an approved work site. A minimum of 54 clock hours per semester of supervised work is required for each unit of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week be distributed throughout the semester. Instructor approval required. A maximum of three units can be earned for this course.

title: History of Jazz
description: A survey of jazz as a significant American art form from its roots in African music to the present. Major styles, leading performers, significant compositions and recordings, and the social, economic, and cultural contexts of the music will be stressed.

title: World Music
description: Examines the dominant musical cultures of the world within Africa, the Americas, Europe, and Asia and compares these to Western popular music. Identifies vocal and instrumental genres within selected cultures and examines the harmonic, melodic, and rhythmic characteristics of each style. Lectures, films, recordings, and media presentations will assist the student in exploring the ways in which music is used around the world for aesthetic, social, and spiritual purposes.

title: American Folk Music
description: The study of American folk music by both region and period. Instruction will include lecture, reading, and listening assignments, and various audio-visual materials. No previous musical experience required.

title: American Folk Music - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: The study of American folk music by both region and period. Instruction will include lecture, reading, and listening assignments, and various audio-visual materials. No previous musical experience required. An honors course designed to provide an enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 14B and MUS 14BH .

title: Rock Music History and Appreciation
description: Historical survey of rock music from its beginnings in the early 1950s to the present. Rhythm and blues, rockabilly, the British Invasion, Motown, soul, folk rock, hard rock, punk, metal, and various alternative rock styles will be discussed. Personalities and musical styles will be related to the sociology of the time period being studied.

title: Rock Music History and Appreciation - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: Historical survey of rock music from its beginnings in the early 1950s to the present. Rhythm and blues, rockabilly, the British Invasion, Motown, soul, folk rock, hard rock, punk, metal, and various alternative rock styles will be discussed. Personalities and musical styles will be related to the sociology of the time period being studied. An honors course designed to provide enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 15 and MUS 15H .

title: Elementary Voice
description: Group singing instruction with an emphasis on breathing, posture, performance techniques, and vocal quality. English and American songs are studied and performed.

title: Intermediate Voice
description: Group and individual instruction concentrating on individual vocal development and emphasizing singing techniques required for singing popular, theatrical, and classical music. Includes singing in foreign languages.

title: Advanced Voice
description: Group and individual study of the style, techniques, and interpretation of art songs and songs from operas and musicals. Emphasis will be placed on diction and pronunciation in Italian, German, and French.

title: Conducting
description: Beat patterns, score reading, and rehearsal techniques for conducting. Includes techniques needed for group direction and leadership.

title: Elementary Guitar
description: Group lesson learning environment for the development of beginning level performance skills on the acoustic guitar. Note reading, hand positions, chords, strumming, finger picking, and improvisation will be covered. Students must furnish their own acoustic guitars.

title: Intermediate Guitar
description: Techniques for reading and playing music arranged for the solo guitar. Students must furnish their own acoustic guitar.

title: Advanced Guitar
description: Style, technique, and interpretation of guitar music of the 18th and 19th centuries. Includes sight reading and ensemble playing. Students must furnish their own acoustic guitars.

title: Jazz Improvisation
description: Styles and techniques of jazz improvisation. Students must furnish their own musical instruments to play for and with the class.

title: Advanced Jazz Improvisation
description: Advanced techniques of jazz improvisation. Includes minor, dominant, and pentatonic scales along with arpeggiating polychords, altered chords, chord progressions, and 32-bar jazz standards. Students must furnish their instruments and be able to perform individually and with the class.

title: Chamber Music
description: Select ensemble of winds, strings, guitar, and percussion instrumentalists specializing in the performance of chamber music from the medieval period to the present. The course may include brass quintets, woodwind quintets, saxophone quartets, and mixed instrumental ensembles of two through twenty performers. Students must have previous instrumental experience and pass an entrance audition during the first week of instruction. Public performances on campus and in the community are required. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Choral Workshop
description: Choral music of all genres with an emphasis on strengthening choral skills, including sight singing, tone, blend, balance and good vocal technique. Covers choral tone of the Renaissance to correct use of the microphone when singing pop or vocal jazz. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice. Open to all students without an audition.

title: Advanced Choral Workshop
description: Choral music of all genres with an emphasis on strengthening advanced choral skills, including advanced sight singing, tone, blend, balance and advanced vocal technique. Covers advanced knowledge and use of choral tone of the Renaissance to advanced use of the microphone when singing pop or vocal jazz. Students who repeat this course will improve advanced skills through further instruction and practice. Admission by audition.

title: Collegiate Chorale
description: This course is for the study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate for a non-auditioned choral ensemble with an emphasis in the development of skills needed to perform with a choral ensemble consisting of individuals with little or no prior choral experience. A variety of mixed choral repertoire will be studied and performed, from music of the Renaissance to contemporary Pop, Broadway, and Vocal Jazz. Rehearsal time will also be devoted to vocal development and improving music theory skills. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Attendance at performances is required.

title: Concert Choir
description: This course is for the study, rehearsal, and performance of repertoire suited for a large mixed choral ensemble. The repertoire will draw from a variety of styles, time periods, and cultures and may include major choral works. Different literature will be studied each semester. Sight singing skills and proper vocal technique are emphasized. Voice placement auditions are held the first week of class. Attendance at all performances including those off-site is required. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice. Simple auditions held first week of the semester.

title: Advanced Concert Choir
description: This course is for the study, rehearsal, and performance of advanced repertoire suited for a large mixed choral ensemble. The advanced repertoire will draw from a variety of styles, time periods, and cultures and may include major choral works. Different advanced literature will be studied each semester. Advanced sight singing skills and proper vocal technique are emphasized. Voice placement auditions are held the first week of class. Attendance at all performances including those off-campus is required. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further advanced instruction and practice. Admission by audition, auditions held first week of the semester.

title: Opera Scenes
description: Preparation and public performance of scenes from various operas, or a complete opera, with piano accompaniment. Opportunities for performing principal roles and opera chorus. Emphasis on healthy vocal production, projection, effective story-telling and communication of text, diction and correct pronunciation of English and foreign languages, characterization, stage deportment, and dance. Students who repeat this course will continue to improve and refine these skills through further instruction and stage experience. Audition required.

title: Women's Vocal Ensemble

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Admission by audition during the first week of class

description: This ensemble is for the study, rehearsal and public performance of treble voiced choral literature with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform within a specialized ensemble. Repertoire selected throughout the year will include music from different time periods, languages, and styles. Different literature will be studied each semester. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Attendance is required at all public performances including off-campus locations. Auditions held the first week.

title: Wind Symphony
description: Study, rehearsal, and performance of concert wind band literature in a medium to large ensemble format. Students must have previous instrumental training on a standard band instrument. Public performance in both on and off-campus venues required. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice. Audition required.

title: Ensemble

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Ability to read music or admission by audition.

description: This course is for the study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate to the ensemble, with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform within a specialized ensemble, namely chamber instrumentation, also including percussion, guitar, and piano ensembles. In addition, ensembles particular to Jazz genres would be included, such as combo instrumental ensembles and specialized vocal arrangement ensembles. Different literature will be studied each semester. Choice of ensemble is based on each student's identified major instrument or voice. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. On campus performances may be required.

title: Laboratory Band
description: Study and performance of improvisation, jazz, and pop music of all types. Open to all students with prior instrumental experience. Audition may be required.

title: Vocal Jazz Ensemble
description: This course is for the study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate for an intermediate vocal jazz ensemble. This group will perform vocal jazz charts accompanied by a rhythm section, as well as a cappella pieces. Topics of study will include basics of singing jazz, vocal improvisation, group singing techniques, and microphone techniques. The ensemble will perform locally and/or at vocal jazz festivals. Attendance at performances and competitions is required. Different literature will be studied each semester. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation.

title: Advanced Vocal Jazz Ensemble
description: This course is for the advanced study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate for an advanced vocal jazz ensemble. This group will perform advanced vocal jazz charts accompanied by a rhythm section, as well as advanced a cappella pieces. Topics of study will include advanced jazz singing, advanced vocal improvisation, advanced group singing techniques, and continued effective microphone techniques. The ensemble will perform in the local community and at vocal jazz festivals. Off-campus attendance at performances and competitions is required. Different complex literature will be studied each semester. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Admission by audition each Fall semester.

title: Chamber Singers
description: This course is for the study, rehearsal, and public performance of advanced choral repertoire with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform difficult and challenging choral pieces. A wide variety of choral literature is performed publicly several times each semester, and a performance tour occurs each spring semester. Emphasizes advanced musical skills and vocal techniques while focusing on the importance of blend, balance, and tone. Auditions for this course are held each May. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Off-campus performances are required.

title: Advanced Chamber Singers
description: This course is for the advanced study, rehearsal, and public performance of more advanced choral repertoire with an emphasis on the development of advanced skills needed to perform difficult and challenging choral pieces. A wide variety of complex choral literature is performed publicly several times each semester, and a performance tour occurs each spring semester. Emphasizes more advanced musical skills and vocal techniques while focusing on the importance of blend, balance, and tone. Auditions for this course are held each May. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Off-campus performances are required.

title: Jazz Ensemble
description: Study and performance of jazz and big band music. Provides an opportunity to learn techniques applicable to the large jazz ensemble. Off-campus public performance required. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice. Admission by audition.

title: Men's Vocal Ensemble

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Admission by audition the first week of class

description: This course is for the study, rehearsal and performance of repertoire suited for a men's choral ensemble. The repertoire will be drawn from a variety of styles and time periods. Different literature will be studied each semester. Attendance is required at all public performances including off-campus locations. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Auditions held the first week.

title: Wind Ensemble
description: The premiere classical wind and percussion ensemble at the College. Students must have previous musical training, a standard band instrument, and pass an entrance audition. A variety of wind band repertoire will be studied and performed, from music of the medieval period to contemporary compositions. Public performances on campus and in the community are required each semester, and a concert tour may be included. Opportunities to conduct, arrange and compose music, and perform as a soloist may be provided to capable students. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Advanced Wind Ensemble
description: Advanced performance level for the premiere classical wind and percussion ensemble at the College. Students must have previous musical training, a standard band instrument, and pass an entrance audition. A variety of wind band repertoire will be studied and performed, from music of the medieval period to contemporary compositions. Public performances on campus and in the community are required each semester, and a concert tour may be included. Opportunities to conduct, arrange and compose music, and perform as a soloist may be provided to capable students. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice, at the advanced level.

title: Jazz Improvisation and Performance Choir
description: For information regarding auditions, contact instructor. This course is for the study, rehearsal, and public performance of advanced vocal jazz literature with an emphasis on improvisation and skills needed to perform within a highly select vocal jazz ensemble.

title: Contemporary A Cappella Ensemble
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of contemporary a cappella music with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform using microphones in a small a cappella setting. Different literature studied each semester. Ensemble specializing in a cappella performances of current rock, pop, jazz, and country hits. Topics include instrumental emulation, vocal percussion microphone techniques, choreography, pop and jazz solo techniques, and arranging. Off campus performances may be required. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation.

title: Advanced Contemporary A Cappella Ensemble
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of advanced contemporary a cappella music with an emphasis on the development of advanced skills needed to perform using microphones in a small a cappella setting. Different advanced literature studied each semester. Ensemble specializing in a cappella performances of current rock, pop, jazz, and country hits. Topics include advanced techniques in instrumental emulation, vocal percussion microphone techniques, choreography, pop and jazz solo techniques, and arranging. Off campus performances may be required. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Admission by audition.

title: Madrigal Singers
description: The study, rehearsal, and public performance of early polyphonic choral literature, with an emphasis on the development of skills need to perform with a small, elite, choral ensemble. The primary focus is on literature from the Medieval and Renaissance periods. The number of singers is limited as to conform to performance practices of that time period. Different literature will be studied each semester. Concerts will be performed each semester at Mt SAC along with possible performance tours. Singers focus on proper vocal technique, sight singing, blending and balancing within the choir, and singing in foreign languages. Auditions will be held at the beginning of each semester.

title: String Ensemble
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate to string ensembles and strings chamber music, with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform within this type of specialized ensemble, and the individual and ensemble techniques relevant to the instruments of the string family (violin, viola, cello, or bass). Different repertoire will be studied each semester. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Audition is required. Off-campus concerts are possible.

title: Percussion Ensemble
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate to percussion ensembles and percussion chamber music, with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform within this type of specialized ensemble, and the individual and ensemble techniques relevant to the instruments of the percussion family (including timpani, marimba, xylophone, drums, and auxiliary percussion). Different repertoire will be studied each semester. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Audition is required.

title: Guitar Ensemble
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate to guitar ensembles and guitar chamber music, with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform within this type of specialized ensemble, and the individual and ensemble techniques relevant to the guitar. Different repertoire will be studied each semester. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Audition is required.

title: Woodwind Ensemble
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate to woodwind ensembles and woodwind chamber music, with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform within this type of specialized ensemble, and the individual and ensemble techniques relevant to the woodwind family (including piccolo, flute, clarinet, bass clarinet, oboe, bassoon, and saxophones). Different repertoire will be studied each semester. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Audition is required. Off campus concerts may be required.

title: Brass Ensemble
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of literature appropriate to brass ensembles and brass chamber music, with an emphasis on the development of skills needed to perform within this type of specialized ensemble, and the individual and ensemble techniques relevant to the instruments of the brass family (trumpet, trombone, French horn, euphonium, and/or tuba). Different repertoires will be studied each semester. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Audition required.

title: Marching Band Winds
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of music and movement appropriate to wind instruments in a marching band. On- and off-campus performances. Admission by audition. Emphasis is placed on development of the expressive, technical, musical, and physical skills required to execute musical and movement drills in real time. Memorization of field shows is required; Repertoire and movement drills vary by semester.

title: Marching Band Percussion
description: Study, rehearsal, and public performance of music and movement appropriate to percussion in a marching band. Emphasis is placed on development drumming rudiments, along with the expressive, technical, musical, and physical skills required to execute musical and movement drills in real time, performing in a drum line or front ensemble. Memorization of field shows is required. Repertoire and movement drills vary by semester. On- and off-campus performances. Admission by audition.

title: Success for Musicians
description: Practice habits, self-scheduling techniques, achieving artistry, balancing personal and social roles, finding musical flow, setting and achieving goals, music as "play" versus music as "work", self-concepts, and values.

title: Special Projects in Music
description: Offered to selected students in recognition of academic interests and abilities to give them the opportunity to explore these interests and abilities in greater depth. The content of each course and the methods of study vary from semester to semester and depend on the particular project under consideration. Students must have an instructor's approval before enrolling in this course. Projects must be approved in advance.

title: Introduction to Western Classical Music
description: Survey of art music in western civilization. Topics studied include but are not limited to elements of music, basic musical forms, music periods, styles, and the role of music and musicians in the western world. Attending at least one live concert is required.

title: Introduction to Western Classical Music - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: Survey of art music in western civilization. Topics studied include but are not limited to elements of music, basic musical forms, music periods, styles, and the role of music and musicians in the western world. Attending at least one live concert is required. An honors course designed to provide an enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 100 and MUS 100H .

title: Women in Music
description: A survey of art music in Western civilization with attention to gender issues, specifically in terms of women in music - as creators, performers, patrons, and listeners - from an historical perspective. Topics include elements of music, critical listening skills, time periods in music history (Medieval to 21st Century), musical styles, music as an expressive art form, and specific composers and musicians whose work speaks to gender-related issues. Appropriate for non-music majors. Attending at least one live concert is required.

title: Film Music Appreciation
description: A study of American film music from 1927 to present day, Comprehensive lectures include a historical analysis of the evolution of the art form, introduction of prominent film composers, and analysis of various score styles. Students will be required to access, watch, and listen to several films throughout the course.

title: Music and Culture of Hip Hop
description: Introduction to the ideological, social, historical, and cultural influences on hip hop in African and African American history. Course addresses controversies surrounding rap music including violence, sexism, and racial stereotyping. Topics include early success of hip hop, its spread to mainstream culture, growth of "gangsta rap," and the commercial success of rap.

title: Music and Culture of Hip-Hop - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: Introduction to the ideological, social, historical and cultural influences on hip hop in African and African American history. Course addresses controversies surrounding rap music including violence, sexism, and racial stereotyping. Topics include early success of hip hop, its spread to mainstream culture, growth of "gangsta rap," and the commercial success of rap. An honors course designed to provide an enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 103 and MUS 103H .

title: Western Music History I: Antiquity to 1750
description: Survey of music history and literature from antiquity to 1750, including cultural, intellectual and social influences, and provides an in-depth examination of the development of Western European music through analysis and synthesis of historical details and stylistic elements of the musical trends of the era. Lectures are augmented by sound recordings. Attending a live concert may be required.

title: Western Music History II: 1750 to Present
description: Survey of music history and literature from 1750 to the present, including cultural, intellectual, and social influences. This course provides an in-depth examination of the development of Western European music through analysis and synthesizing of historical details and stylistic elements of the musical trends of the era. Attending at least one live concert is required.

title: Music Fundamentals
description: Introduction to the notation and fundamental theoretical elements of Western music, demonstrated through a variety of styles, past and current. Students will engage music through listening, reading, lecture, writing, and performance. Topics include music notation, pitch, rhythm, tonality, scales, key signatures, intervals, chords, melody, harmony, and form, as well as linguistic, cognitive, and mathematical frameworks for understanding how music works.

title: Music Fundamentals for Musicians
description: Introduction to the notation and fundamental theoretical elements of Western music through listening, analysis, singing, rhythm performance, and dictation. Includes modern staff notation, scales and modes, intervals, tertian harmony, and Roman numeral analysis, as well as the development of sight-singing, rhythm reading, and dictation skills. Intended for students with prior experience in musical performance or composition. Required for students pursuing Audio Arts, Commercial Music, and Music Studies degrees and/or certificates.

title: Music Theory I

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MUS 110A or satisfactory score on Music Theory Placement Examination
Corequisite: MUS 125 (may have been taken previously)

description: Harmony and form as practiced in Western tonal music. Listening, composition, and analysis of music to cover topics including Roman numeral theory, diatonic chord syntax, counterpoint, and chorale-style part writing with diatonic triads.

title: Musicianship I

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: MUS 110A or satisfactory score on Musicianship Placement Examination
Corequisite: MUS 120 (may have been taken previously)

description: Audiation of the rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic aspects of music through sight singing, rhythm reading, and dictation. Covers divisional rhythms, diatonic melodies, and primary chord progressions.

title: Music Theory II

requirements.raw: Corequisite: ( MUS 135 or MUS 6A) (May have been taken previously)

description: Harmony and form as practiced in Western tonal music. Listening, composition, and analysis of music to cover topics including non-chord tones, secondary functions, modulation, period forms, small forms, and chromatic part writing with seventh chords and suspensions.

title: Musicianship II

requirements.raw: Corequisite: ( MUS 130 or MUS 3B) (may have been taken previously)

description: Audiation of the rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic aspects of music through sight singing, rhythm reading, and dictation. Covers subdivisional rhythms, chromatic melodies, and diatonic chord progressions.

title: Music Theory III

requirements.raw: Corequisite: ( MUS 145 or MUS 6B) (may have been taken previously)

description: Harmony and form as practiced in Western tonal music. Listening, composition, and analysis of music to cover topics including mode mixture, the Neapolitan, augmented-sixth chords, altered dominants, linear chromaticism, sonata form theory, and part writing with advanced chromaticism.

title: Musicianship III

requirements.raw: Corequisite: ( MUS 140 or MUS 3C) (May have been taken previously)

description: Audiation of the rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic aspects of music through sight singing, rhythm reading, and dictation. Covers syncopated rhythms, modulating melodies, and chromatic chord progressions.

title: Music Theory IV

requirements.raw: Corequisite: MUS 155 (may have been taken previously)

description: Pitch, rhythm, and harmony in late-Romantic and post-tonal Western music. Listening, composition, and analysis of music to cover topics including enharmonic reinterpretation, chromatic mediants, synthetic scales, non-tertian harmony, set theory, and serialism.

title: Musicianship IV

requirements.raw: Corequisite: MUS 150 (may have been taken previously)

description: Audiation of the rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic aspects of music through sight singing, rhythm reading, and dictation. Covers polyrhythms, irregular meters, post-tonal melodies, and non-tertian chords.

title: Individual Instruction

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Admission by audition and concurrent participation in an appropriate ensemble.

description: Applied music for students also enrolled in a major performing group. Instruction includes a private one-half hour lesson per week. Individual problems of performance techniques, interpretation, and repertoire are included. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further instruction and practice.

title: Applied Music for Major I
description: Designed for the beginning music major. Consists of 15 one-hour individualized study of repertoire for the specific instrument or voice through private instruction. Participation in weekly studio classes, weekly progress check on assigned repertoire, and end-of-semester jury performance. Emphasis on progressive development of skills needed for solo performance needed for transfer as a music major. Evaluation through a juried performance. Admission by audition.

title: Applied Music for Major II
description: Designed for the music major who is preparing for transfer auditions; schedule consists of 14 one-hour individualized lessons for the study of repertoire for the specific instrument or voice through. Participation in weekly studio classes, weekly progress check on assigned repertoire, and end-of-semester jury performance. Emphasis on progressive development of skills needed for solo performance needed for transfer as a music major. Evaluation through a juried performance. Admission by audition.

title: Piano I
description: Introduction to beginning keyboard skills, including notation. Includes basic technique, major and minor five finger patterns, major scales, sight reading, and basic chord progressions as they are encountered in beginning piano music. No prior musical experience is required.

title: Piano II
description: Development and refinement of piano skills through late-beginner and early-intermediate piano music. Includes damper pedal technique, major and minor scales and patterns, arpeggios, transposition, and the harmonization of melodies using primary chords.

title: Piano III
description: Development and refinement of piano skills through intermediate piano music. Includes major and minor scales and arpeggios, sight-reading, expanded chord progressions, transposition, and the harmonization of melodies using primary and secondary chords.

title: Jazz and Pop Piano I
description: Developing and refining keyboard skills through upper-beginning and early intermediate jazz and pop music. Includes piano technique, major and minor scales, arpeggios, sight-reading, chord progressions, harmonization, and transposition. Other topics include interpretation of basic chord symbols, Roman numeral notation, and basic jazz and pop voicings for accompanying in ballad, swing, and bossa nova styles.

title: Functional Keyboard Skills
description: This course develops comprehensive keyboard and collaborative piano skills through four main areas: accompaniment, sight-reading, technical facility, and solo performance. Students will master two-hand accompaniments for vocal and instrumental repertoire, sight-read four-part chorales and open scores, perform scales and arpeggios in specified major/minor keys, and prepare intermediate- to advanced-level solo repertoire. The course culminates in a formal accompaniment recital where students demonstrate their collaborative musicianship. Emphasis is placed on practical applications of keyboard skills including harmonization using primary and secondary chords, transposition, ensemble playing, and appropriate accompaniment styles such as Alberti bass and waltz patterns.

title: Jazz and Pop Piano II
description: Developing and refining keyboard skills through jazz and popular music. Includes piano technique, major and minor scales, arpeggios, sight-reading, chord progressions, harmonization, and transposition. Other topics include interpretation of advanced chord symbols, Roman numeral notation, and intermediate jazz and pop voicings for accompanying in ballad, swing, and bossa nova styles.

title: DJ Performance
description: The study, rehearsal, and public performance of Disc Jockeyed (DJ) music and Electronic Dance Music (EDM). Styles include but are not limited to Pop, House, Techno, Trap, Hip Hop, Dubstep, Glitch, Ambient, and Drum and Bass. The skills needed to perform live in DJ and EDM settings will be emphasized. Performers will work collaboratively to put on performances that feature realtime collaboration and integration of industry-standard technologies to produce modern dance-music experiences. Different literature will be studied each semester based on the ensemble composition. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Admission by audition.

title: Pop/Rock Band
description: The study, rehearsal, and public performance of commercial music in band configurations. Styles covered will include but are not limited to Pop, Rock, R&B, Country, and Hip Hop. The skills needed to perform live in commercial music settings will be emphasized. Combos will be made up of voice, guitar, keyboard, bass, drum-set, and other traditional instruments. Different literature will be studied each semester based on the ensemble composition. This course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Admission by audition.

title: Advanced Commercial Music Ensemble
description: The study, rehearsal, and public performance of advanced-level and experimental commercial music. Genres covered will include Pop, Rock, Hip Hop, Country, Rhythm and Blues, Disc Jockeyed, Electronic Dance, and Experimental Music. This ensemble will focus on emerging techniques that integrate traditional live performance with modern controllerism using a variety of Musical Instrument Digital Interfaces. Students are required to have significant instrumental, vocal and/or disc jockey performance skills. Students will host and perform in innovative musical and multimedia experiences in a variety of settings. The course is repeatable for credit the maximum times allowable by regulation. Admission by audition.

title: Jazz and Commercial Arranging
description: This course teaches the fundamentals of jazz and commercial arranging via analysis and written assignments. The class focuses on learning the tools necessary to arrange in unison, two-part, four- and five-part closed and open voicings, utilizing tight intervals between consecutive voice-parts.

title: Applied Music Audition Preparation
description: Advanced applied music for students also enrolled in a major performing group. Instruction includes a private one-half hour lesson per week. Concentration on preparation for commercial and educational transfer auditions. Advanced performance techniques, advanced interpretation, and advanced repertoire are included. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further advanced instruction and practice.

title: Applied Music Recital Preparation
description: Advanced applied music for students also enrolled in a major performing group. Instruction includes a private one-half hour lesson per week. Concentration on preparation for a recital to take place in the same semester. Advanced performance techniques, advanced interpretation, and advanced repertoire are included. Students who repeat this course will improve skills through further advanced instruction and practice.

title: Introduction to Native American Studies
description: An introductory survey to the interdisciplinary analysis of the historical, socio-political, economic, educational, and cultural experiences, conditions, and influences related to Indigenous Peoples in what is now called the United States. The course examines key topics from an Indigenous Peoples' perspective, such as: Colonialism, settler colonialism, racialization, domination, Indigeneity, sovereignty, de-culturalization, hegemony, land, self-determination, agency, resistance, social movements, decolonization, anti-racism, and the intersection of racial, ethnic, gender, and sexual identities.

title: Nursing Work Experience Program

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course.

description: Supervised work experience in the field of Nursing that connects academic learning with hands-on experience in the workplace. Designed to provide an integrated instructional program supporting students' educational and career goals. A minimum of 54 hours of paid or unpaid work per unit is required.

title: The Nursing Process I

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ANAT 10A and ANAT 10B ) or ( ANAT 35 and ANAT 36 ) and ( MICR 1 or MICR 22 ) and ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A and admission to the nursing program.

description: Principles of nursing as related to a culturally diverse population, adulthood through senescence. Theory and application of the Nursing Process including meaning of illness, promoting health patterns, hygiene, safety, asepsis, medication administration, elimination, communication.

title: The Nursing Process II
description: Principles of nursing as related to a culturally diverse population, adulthood through senescence. Theory and application of the Nursing Process including oxygenation, perfusion, legal/ethical aspects, comfort, fluid and electrolytes, spirituality, and nursing trends.

title: Pharmacology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Eligibility for ( STAT C1000 or MATH 110) or (STAT C1000H or MATH 110H)

description: Pharmacology, the ethical and legal responsibilities in the administration of medications. Principles of administration of various dosage forms, cultural influences, the nursing process, drug therapy, and mathematical computations are presented. Resources for locating pharmacological information are stressed.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Locomotion/Sensory/Integument/Oncology/Immunology

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( NURS 101 or NURS 1B) and ( NURS 102 or NURS 2) or ( NURS 200 or NURS 70)

description: Application and concepts for nursing assessment and intervention for clients with problems of locomotion, sensation, and integument. Introductions to oncology nursing and immunology nursing are included.

title: Maternal-Newborn Nursing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( NURS 113 or NURS 3) or ( NURS 200 or NURS 70)

description: Concepts of anatomy, physiology, and fetal growth and development applied to the care of maternity patients, newborn infants, and their families. Nursing care on a wellness-illness continuum using the family-centered approach is introduced.

title: Pediatric Nursing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( NURS 114 or NURS 4) or ( CHLD 10 or CHLD 10H or PSYC 14 or PSYC 14H )

description: Concepts of nursing assessment and intervention with application to pediatric clients.

title: Role Transition

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Nursing: Licensed Psychiatric Technician (LPT) to Registered Nurse (RN) Option or Nursing: Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) to Registered Nurse (RN) Option and ( ANAT 10A and ANAT 10B or ANAT 35 and ANAT 36 ) and ( CHLD 10 or CHLD 10H or PSYC 14 or PSYC 14H ) and ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A or ENGL C1000H or ENGL C1000H or AMLA 1A ) and ( MICR 1 or MICR 22 ) and ( PSYC C1000 or PSYC 1A or PSYC C1000H or PSYC 1AH)

description: For the Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN), Psychiatric Technician (PT), or advanced placement student transitioning into the role of the Registered Nurse (RN).

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Nutrition/Elimination/ Surgical Asepsis
description: Concepts for nursing assessment and intervention with application to clients with problems of nutrition, elimination, and the reproductive systems. Clients in pre-, intra- and post-operative settings are included.

title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( PSYC C1000 or PSYC 1A or PSYC C1000H or PSYC 1AH) and ( NURS 206 or NURS 7)

description: Concepts of nursing assessment and intervention with application to clients with psychiatric disorders in a mental health setting. Concepts of mental health and illness are presented within the Nursing Process. Theories of personality development and effective coping strategies for all stages of the life cycle from childhood through senescence are included.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Perfusion and Oxygenation
description: Concepts for nursing assessment and interventions with application to clients with perfusion and oxygenation problems.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Integration/Regulation
description: Presentation and application of concepts of nursing assessment to develop the cognitive and psychomotor skills necessary to provide nursing intervention for clients with neurological and endocrine disturbances using the Nursing Process. Emphasis is on clients from early adulthood through senescence. Application of knowledge from sciences to understanding pathophysiology is emphasized. Leadership and management experiences are included.

title: Preceptorship in Nursing

requirements.raw: Corequisite: NURS 211 or NURS 10 (may have been taken previously)

description: Students develop cognitive and leadership skills for a pre-licensed preceptee position and prepare for professional responsibilities in employment under the direct supervision of a qualified Registered Nurse. Includes explanation and analysis of current trends and issues in nursing.

title: Introduction to Nutrition as a Career

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: NF 10 or NF 25 or NF 25H

description: Careers in nutrition, dietetics, and clinical food service. Includes program requirements for nutrition and dietetics majors, career opportunities, professional organizations, ethics, and career preparation. Students should be considering a major or career in nutrition, dietetics, nutrition science, or clinical food service.

title: Nutrition for Health and Wellness
description: Principles of nutrition and their relationship to optimum health and wellness. Emphasizes nutrient needs, food selection, and weight control during the various life stages from prenatal to adult. Student food intake is evaluated several ways including computer diet analysis. This course is intended for non-health science majors.

title: Sports Nutrition
description: Principles of nutrition are studied and applied to the athlete and active individuals. Includes macro and micro nutrient intakes, hydration, pre and post event food choices, supplements and ergogenic aids, body composition, weight loss/gain. This course also examines the cultural, sociological, and psychological influences related to nutrition, fitness and athletic achievement.

title: Principles of Foods with Laboratory
description: Application of food science principles with emphasis on ingredient function and interaction, food preparation techniques, sensory evaluation standards, food safety and sanitation, and nutrient composition of food.

title: Introduction to Nutrition Science
description: Scientific concepts of nutrition related to the function of nutrients in basic life processes and current health issues with emphasis on dietary requirements of the individual. Students will explore scientific inquiry and apply critical thinking and scientific principles to analyze and evaluate nutrition information while learning foundational principles of nutrition science. Integrates concepts from biology, biochemistry, microbiology, physiology, anatomy, and psychology to learn about the interactions between dietary intake and the human body. Topics include functions and sources of nutrients; Dietary Guidelines and current nutrition recommendations; digestion, absorption, and metabolism of nutrients; and health, fitness, and disease. Students will utilize an information database to analyze dietary intake.

title: Introduction to Nutrition Science - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: Scientific concepts of nutrition related to the function of nutrients in basic life processes and current health issues with emphasis on dietary requirements of the individual. Students will explore scientific inquiry and apply critical thinking and scientific principles to analyze and evaluate nutrition information while learning foundational principles of nutrition science. Integrates concepts from biology, biochemistry, microbiology, physiology, anatomy, and psychology to learn about the interactions between dietary intake and the human body. Topics include functions and sources of nutrients; Dietary Guidelines and current nutrition recommendations; digestion, absorption, and metabolism of nutrients; and health, fitness, and disease. Students will utilize an information database to analyze dietary intake. An honors course designed to provide an enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both NF 25 and NF 25H .

title: Cultural and Ethnic Foods
description: Regional, ethnic, cultural, religious, historical, and social influences on food patterns and cuisines. Core components include specialized equipment and utensils related to cultures, traditional foods of selected cultures, geographic factors in food availability, and global food issues. Includes in-depth study of a selected culture group.

title: Cultural and Ethnic Foods Laboratory
description: Experiential learning and exploration of culture, cultural nutrition, and ethnic foods in a laboratory setting. Course includes food preparation, cooking, and tasting experiences that reflect various cultural and ethnic foods and dishes. Recipes and introductory cooking methods represent regional, ethnic, cultural, religious, historical, and social influences on global food patterns and cuisines. Sensory evaluation standards and food safety and sanitation techniques applied.

title: Introduction to Food Science Technologies
description: Food chemistry, food processing, and technology and how these affect the color, flavor, texture, aroma and quality of foods. Core components: government regulation of processing and labeling, sensory evaluation, scientific research methods, function of water in foods, pH and acidity, food processing technologies, nutritional labeling, and packaging; dispersion systems, enzyme reactions, food additives, composition and properties of food.

title: Introduction to Therapeutic Diets
description: Principles and indications for the use of therapeutic diet in the treatment of diseases and disorders in the health care setting. Includes review of the Nutrition Care Process, interdisciplinary team scope of practice, screening for nutritional risk, assessment of dietary needs, medical nutrition therapy interventions, food allergies and intolerances, and menu modifications.

title: Menu Planning and Purchasing for Institutional Food Service
description: Introduction to institutional food-service production: Menu development and standardization; forecasting, purchasing, storage, preparation, and service; equipment specification, selection, and maintenance; therapeutic diets including texture and nutrient modifications; information technology in food-service settings including budgeting, cost/inventory control, nutritional analysis, recipe development, production forecasting, and menu production. Client/patient demographic, cultural, socioeconomic, and religious factors are considered.

title: Cooking for Health and Wellness
description: Principles and techniques of meal planning and food preparation to reduce the risk of chronic disease and support optimal health and wellness. Students will learn to prepare flavorful, balanced, and nutritious meals in this course which combines practical cooking techniques with essential nutrition information. Through hands-on cooking sessions and interactive lectures, students will learn the principles of healthy eating and how to prepare meals that support physical and mental well-being. Appropriate for all skill levels, this class is ideal for those looking to make healthier food choices and enhance their culinary skills.

title: Vegetarian Cuisine
description: Principles and techniques of vegetarian cooking and investigation of issues related to vegetarian diets. Through hands-on cooking sessions and interactive lectures, students will explore plant-based ingredients and culinary techniques to create flavorful, balanced, and nutritious meals. Appropriate for all skill levels, this class is ideal for those interested in nutrition, sustainable food practices, and enhancing their culinary skills.

title: Cooking for Athletic and Physical Performance
description: Principles and techniques of meal planning and food preparation to support optimal athletic and physical performance. Content includes development of sport-specific meal plans, analysis of nutrient and fluid requirements, and food preparation skills and techniques. Through hands-on cooking sessions and interactive lectures, students will learn to prepare flavorful, balanced, and nutritious meals to support athletic and physical performance. Appropriate for all skill levels, this class is ideal for athletes, fitness enthusiasts, and those interested in the relationship between diet and performance.

title: Work Experience in Nutrition and Dietetics

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required. Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course.

description: Provides students with on-the-job experience in an approved worksite which is related to classroom-based learning. A minimum of 54 of paid or unpaid clock hours per semester of supervised work in a clinical, community, or long-term nutrition facility is required for each unit of credit. It is recommended that the hours per week be equally distributed throughout the semester. Work experience placement is not guaranteed, but assistance is provided by faculty. Instructor approval required.

title: Work Experience Supervised by a Nutrition Professional

requirements.raw: Corequisite: NF 41 (May have been taken previously)

description: Provides students with field experience under the supervision of a registered dietitian to meet the Dietary Manager certificate requirements. Only students pursuing the Dietary Manager certificate should enroll. A minimum of 54 clock hours per unit of supervised work in an approved clinical, community, or long-term care nutrition facility is required.

title: Work Experience Supervised by a Food Service Professional

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Instructor approval required Students must have completed at least one-third of the units for the related program or be concurrently enrolled in a class in a program related to the work experience course.

description: Provides students with field experience under the supervision of a food service professional to meet the Dietary Manager certificate requirements. Only students pursuing the Dietary Manager certificate should enroll. A minimum of 108 clock hours per semester of supervised work in an approved clinical, community, or long-term care nutrition facility is required.

title: Introduction to Oceanography
description: Geological, chemical, physical, and biological aspects of the Earth's ocean. Plate tectonics, physiography of ocean basins and continental margins, ocean sediment, atmosphere and ocean circulation, waves and tides, coasts, and marine ecology. The companion Oceanography Lab ( OCEA 10L ) is recommended for students needing a lab to transfer to a four-year college or university. Field trip(s) are required.

title: Introduction to Oceanography - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: An honors course designed to provide an enriched experience. Geological, chemical, physical, and biological aspects of the Earth's ocean. Plate tectonics, physiography of ocean basins and continental margins, ocean sediment, atmosphere and ocean circulation, waves and tides, coasts, and marine ecology. The companion Oceanography Lab ( OCEA 10L ) is recommended for students needing a lab to transfer to a 4-year college or university. Field trip(s) required. Students may not receive credit for both OCEA 10 and OCEA 10H .

title: Introduction to Oceanography Laboratory

requirements.raw: Corequisite: OCEA 10 or OCEA 10H (May have been taken previously)

description: Laboratory applications and problem solving in oceanography, including related aspects of geology, physics, chemistry, and marine biology. A hands-on approach to the marine environment and oceanic processes. Recommended for students needing a lab to transfer to a 4-year college or university.

title: The Coastal Ocean
description: Coastal oceanography, geology, biology , and climate science introduced through a series of modules. Includes basic principles and hands-on experiences demonstrating principles. Laboratory studies and overnight field trips to the coast required.

title: Introduction to Paralegal/Legal

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Eligibility for ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: Federal and state legal systems, role of paralegals and relationship of paralegals to attorneys, basic civil litigation, legal writing, investigation of claims, and legal ethics for paralegals.

title: Legal Analysis and Writing

requirements.raw: Corequisite: PLGL 30 (May have been taken previously)

description: Law library for legal research and references including reading and analyzing cases, statutes, constitutions, secondary sources, and preparation of case briefs.

title: Advanced Legal Analysis and Writing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: PLGL 30 and ( PLGL 31 or PLGL 31A)

description: Research memoranda, trial briefs, appellate briefs, and other legal document preparation. Westlaw and Lexis-Nexis training.

title: Civil Procedure

requirements.raw: Corequisite: PLGL 30 (May have been taken previously)

description: Pre-trial procedural steps of litigating a cause of action to post-trial remedies. Jurisdiction, venue, parties, default judgments, pleadings, and pretrial law and motion. Discovery, summary judgments, settlements and preparation for and support at trial, including post-trial remedies and enforcement of judgments.

title: Law Office Procedures

requirements.raw: Corequisite: PLGL 30 (may have been taken previously)

description: Procedures utilized by a paralegal in a law office. Court systems, preparation and filing of legal papers and court documents, and drafting specialized documents in estate planning, real estate, divorce, unlawful detainer, adoption, corporations, conservatorships, and guardianships.

title: Law Office Technology
description: Personal computer usage for special purposes in the law office. Drafting of legal documents, document control, e-filing, e-discovery, preparation of billing, law office and case load management, and trial graphics and preparation.

title: Paralegal Internship

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: PLGL 31 and PLGL 33 and PLGL 34 and Instructor approval and Compliance with Work Experience regulations as designated in the College Catalog.
Corequisite: PLGL 32 and PLGL 35 and PLGL 37 and PLGL 39 (All may have been taken previously)

description: On-the-job experience in the paralegal profession, which relates to student's classroom based learning. Placement is not guaranteed but assistance is provided by the paralegal faculty. A minimum of five hours per week of supervised work (minimum 54 clock hours per semester) is required.

title: Tort Law
description: Analysis of the law of torts, including intentional torts such as assault, battery, false imprisonment, defamation, privacy, trespass, and nuisance; negligence; and strict liability. Examination of insurance defense issues.

title: Employment and Ethical Issues in Paralegalism

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: PLGL 31 and PLGL 33 and PLGL 34
Corequisite: PLGL 32 and PLGL 35 and PLGL 37 and PLGL 39 (All may have been taken previously)

description: Job search skills including preparation of professional resumes and cover letters, interviewing techniques, networking, application of these skills in beginning the search for paralegal employment, and paralegal and attorney ethics.

title: Contract Law
description: Laws relating to the formation of contracts. Includes study of the Statute of Frauds, third-party rights, liability for breach of contract, remedies, discharge, and the Uniform Commercial Code.

title: Property Law
description: Examination of the law relating to real and personal property. Analysis of the various forms of ownership of real property; easements, covenants, conditions, and licenses; constitutional questions; types of real estate deeds; and land use controls.

title: Family Law
description: Laws relating to marriage, dissolution, nullity, and legal separation. Includes topics of community property, child custody, child support, spousal support, and prenuptial and antenuptial agreements.

title: Wills and Trusts
description: Legal principles of the laws of wills and trusts, organization, and jurisdiction of the California Probate Courts, estate planning and estate taxes.

title: Bankruptcy Law
description: Creation, scope, and administrative function of federal bankruptcy proceedings, including Chapter 7, 11, and 13 cases.

title: Criminal Law and Procedures
description: General principles of criminal law and procedure, elements of crimes against person and property, parties to a crime, defenses to crimes. Analysis of procedural law relating to arrest, search and seizure, rights to counsel and a jury, evidentiary issues, sentencing, and appeal.

title: Evidence Law
description: Evidence law in civil and criminal cases: principles of relevance and competence of evidence, hearsay and character evidence rules, evidentiary privileges, use and authentication of writings. Use of evidence at trial, burdens of proof and presumptions, constitutional issues.

title: The Litigation Practice and eDiscovery
description: Role of eDiscovery in modern day litigation, court rules and procedure, overview of the Electronic Discovery Reference Model (EDRM) process, data privacy laws, and related ethical issues.

title: Project Management Principles in eDiscovery
description: Project management, review of the lifecycle of litigation, and application of project management principles to eDiscovery.

title: Litigation Support Technology from Data Collection to Trial
description: Role of the litigation lifecycle from data collection, document review, and production to use at trial. Role of technology and litigation support department and teams in the acquisition of data and eDiscovery processing.

title: Litigation Support Applications
description: Use of litigation support software and technology in the forensic data collection process and eDiscovery. Practical training in contemporary document review software.

title: Introduction to Logic
description: The use of arguments in ordinary discourse and in academic disciplines within the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences with particular focus on deductive logic. Deductive and inductive reasoning techniques will be critically examined to establish their logical correctness or identify their fallaciousness.

title: Introduction to Logic - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: The use of arguments in ordinary discourse and in academic disciplines within the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences with particular focus on deductive logic. Deductive and inductive reasoning techniques will be critically examined to establish their logical correctness or identify their fallaciousness. An honors course is designed to provide an enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both PHIL 3 and PHIL 3H .

title: Introduction to Symbolic Logic
description: Introduction to the basic elements of modern logic: the nature of arguments, sentence symbolization, truth functions, truth tables, natural deduction, and predicate logic.

title: Introduction to Philosophy
description: Philosophical ideas concerning knowledge, reality, and values. Topics will include the sources and limits of knowledge and the nature of reality. Other topics may include the nature of self, truth, ethics, religion, science, language, beauty and art, political theory, and mind.

title: Introduction to Philosophy - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: Philosophical ideas concerning knowledge, reality, and values. Topics will include the sources and limits of knowledge and the nature of reality. Other topics may include the nature of self, truth, ethics, religion, science, language, beauty and art, political theory, and mind. An honors course is designed to provide an enriched experience. Students may not receive credit for both PHIL 5 and PHIL 5H .

title: Critical Thinking
description: Effective use of critical thinking in contemporary living, including recognizing faulty arguments, the usefulness of validity and truth, and identifying and avoiding common fallacies in thinking.

title: Critical Thinking and Writing

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A

description: This course aims to help students from diverse backgrounds develop good writing skills through learning and applying critical thinking tools in their everyday lives. The critical thinking tools that will be learned in this course include rules from both formal and informal logic, rules for identifying impartial sources to conduct informed research, and rules for writing argumentative essays on topics of interest to students. Among other topics of interest, students are invited to research and write on topics that identify explicit and implicit biases in everyday thinking and speaking, to explore images and discursive forms of representation that help overcome these biases, and to employ research that guides them into forming clear, coherent, and equitable arguments. This course is equivalent to English 1C for transfer and there is a requirement that students write a minimum of 6000 words throughout the semester. This requirement is easily achievable based on a variety of writing assignments included in the course.

title: Critical Thinking and Writing - Honors

requirements.raw: Prerequisite: ( ENGL C1000 or ENGL 1A) or (ENGL C1000H or ENGL 1AH) or AMLA 1A and Acceptance into the Honors Program

description: This course aims to help students from diverse backgrounds develop good writing skills through learning and applying critical thinking tools in their everyday lives. The critical thinking tools that will be learned in this course include rules from both formal and informal logic, rules for identifying impartial sources to conduct informed research, and rules for writing argumentative essays on topics of interest to students. Among other topics of interest, students are invited to research and write on topics that identify explicit and implicit biases in everyday thinking and speaking, to explore images and discursive forms of representation that help overcome these biases, and to employ research that guides them into forming clear, coherent, and equitable arguments.
